title: Link health diag: when a stream cuts in and out, Phosphor says why (client sent late / network gap / hub late), with a Link card graph and Log events
description: Operator 2026-10-09: 'the stream was cutting in and out when I was playing a script, the machine would gracefully handle it and resume ... however I was lost as to what was happening, no log in phosphor showed why'. Likely cause of that session: the trace leak fixed in 96b8893 (segments sent up to 274 ms late; the hub diag showed LATE PLAN 3/min -> 14/min), but Phosphor must tell the user. Wanted: (1) every stream starvation/late-plan episode becomes one Log entry and a status-slot condition with a classified cause: CLIENT (segment left the client late: lead at send under the hub's need), NETWORK (left on time, arrived late or a gap in receipt: from the hub's ingress stamps / ack timing / RTT spike / WS bufferedAmount growth), HUB (arrived on time, planned late: plan_us / LATE PLAN). (2) A Link diagnostics card: RTT and jitter, lead at send (client), arrival lateness (hub), WS buffered amount, frames/s each way, the hub's WiFi RSSI and retry counts if the C6/esp_hosted exposes them, starvation markers on a 2-minute strip. (3) Hub side only if needed: find what the catalog already publishes (stream ingress / sync counters / plan census / link roles in the registry); anything new that a client must read is a Valence RFC (registry roles), not a private field. Acceptance: in valencesim, inject each cause (client stall, network delay via a test proxy, hub late via a forced plan delay) and see the right classification in the Log and the card.
notes:
DESIGN NOTE 2026-10-09 (opus survey; design only, no product code). Scope widened by operator rulings the same day: a HEALTH system in three areas (LINK, THIS DEVICE, MACHINE); the stream-cutout cause (client / network / hub) is the flagship case; NO continuous telemetry: a local health ring plus a per-incident, user-reviewed report (child bead).

== 1. What 2026-10-08 shows (Nucleus/artifacts/diag-20261008-203332.txt, fw 0.1.33, boot 33 at ~18:47) ==
- Stream session joined at 5354 s. Through the stream (~5776 to ~6213 s) the WS never dropped: no reap, no control-stall disconnect, no slot release, no session left. A second client joined at 6254 s, after the stream ended.
- LATE PLAN rose from ~3/min (5776-5850 s) to ~20/min (5999-6050) and ~22/min (6129-6213); one PLANNER STALL at 6195 s ("strip ended 0.6 ms ago"). Nothing else link-related.
- Blind spots, which is why the archive cannot settle it: main.cpp's WIFI_EVENT_STA_DISCONNECTED handler reconnects silently (no log, no count); ESP_LOG output from esp_hosted and wifi is console-only (the geiger bridge carries GLOG lines only, WARN and up to the wire); RSSI is pushed into hub-status every 5 s but never logged; ValenceDevice::onStreamBundle clamps a past-due sample to now (delta < 0 -> 0) without counting it, so late arrival leaves no trace.
- Verdict: the archive rules out a disconnect but cannot separate network from client. If it was the network, it was a connected-but-slow link (WiFi retries, TCP head-of-line), exactly the case that leaves no trace today. The operator's account (it cleared on its own after a while) fits a transient network fault better than the 96b8893 trace leak, which only grows. LATE PLAN alone is not a network signal: it means a re-plan landed after the 4 ms react window (factory react_ms); slow solves cause it, and so can a burst of late bundles landing together.

== 2. Survey: what exists ==
Valence spec and registry:
- CLOCK (SPEC 7.1): RTT and offset. Clients SHOULD resync every 10 s and on an RTT spike over 2x median; clients/js does the 10 s cadence only.
- PROBE/PROBE_REPORT (6.5): one-shot h2c bandwidth and rtt_ms.
- schedule_latency_us (key 49, RFC-059), schedule_horizon_ms (key 50, RFC-087: 250/500/1000, registered "for lookahead players on poor WiFi"), plan.latency, plan.flags (bit1 stretched: the knot lands after its commanded time), plan.start/end/current/elapsed/duration/style roles.
- events.anomaly / anomaly.summary channel roles; anomaly kinds are device labels (no portable "stream starved").
- stream_quiet_release_ms 500 (RFC-098), deadman 600 ms, staleness (RFC-042/051).
- Congestion (10.3) is hub-internal; a client sees it only as an unsolicited GRANT cutting a rate (10.2).
- hub-status 0x0006 is core, its layout unpinned. NO role exists for: hub RSSI, WiFi drops, arrival lateness, late plans, starvation, faults, hub heap.
Nucleus:
- hub-status: heap_free, uptime_s, rssi (i8 dBm, 0 = none, pushed from main.cpp's 5 s loop: each esp_wifi_* call is a ~151 ms esp_hosted RPC), sessions, log_dropped, motor_switch, motor_fault. No roles on them.
- kinetic-diag 0x1111 (72 B, 1 Hz, role anomaly.summary): plans, failures, anomalies, mode, plan_kind, per-kind counters (settle, endvel_clamped, knot_trimmed, dwell_zeroed, knot_refused "late or out of order", piece_over_ceiling), plan_us_last/max/avg, sync_bundles/samples/enqueued/dropped (dropped lumps late, refused, PAUSE and ingress drops), sync_seg_bundles (always 0), reset_gen (always 0).
- motion-anomaly EVENT: the settle edge is the hub's own "stream ran out" marker.
- MotionArbiter counts _late_plans, _planner_stalls, _lease_lapses, tick stalls: none on the wire, only rate-limited GLOGW text in the 0x0008 log.
- No WiFi drop count or reason; no retry counts (no cheap source under esp_hosted; esp_wifi_statis_dump is debug-only). Drive alarm/ready: val-091.73, unbuilt. Board thermistor and fan: console only. No BLE (CONFIG_BT_ENABLED unset).
Phosphor:
- machine.stats: clockOffsetUs, clockRttUs (10 s cadence), lastRxMs, pushesByChannel, render {fps, delayMs, heldPct, skewMs}, reconnects. framesIn/framesOut/bytesIn never move (ph-cmz).
- motion.js filteredHubNowUs: best-bound offset from kept CLOCK exchanges.
- The segments door clips a late start silently (`if (e < hubNow + lat) e = hubNow + lat`): the exact CLIENT-late signal, unreported. Lookahead is half the horizon (125 ms at 250).
- funscript scheduler: observePlan measures plan-start lag end to end (includes the STATE downlink).
- telebuf: p95 arrival gap of the 50 Hz at-rate position telemetry = downlink jitter.
- Unused: ws.bufferedAmount, event-loop lag, heap, long tasks, CPU pressure (soak-player measures them over CDP; its BOUNDS: lagP95 25 ms, heap +8 MB, leadMin 60 ms).
- Log rings machine.events.{log, anomaly, safety, session, nacks}; local lines push {channel: null, channelName, body: {level, tag, message}}.
- Status slot (TopStrip): one thing by priority: link fault, unattended, refusal, jog note, history msg, latch notices, safety edge, virtual, idle.
- hold.js (press and hold, keyboard included); AboutPane is shell only.

== 3. Flagship: the stream cutout, classified ==
Episode opens on (a) hub starvation: RFC role stream.starved increments; until the RFC lands, Phosphor detects it from roles alone: the reported plan has run out (plan.elapsed >= plan.duration, no newer plan) while a span this session sent should be executing, past one hub tick plus half the RTT; or (b) the door clipped a span (CLIENT opens even when the hub rode it out). Evidence window W = 1 s before the edge (hub time converted with the CLOCK offset). Same-cause episodes within 10 s merge.
First match wins:
1. CLIENT. Decider: lead at send, measured in the door per bundle (first start minus filtered hub now). Threshold: any clip in W, or lead_send_min(W) < need, need = schedule_latency_us + 5 ms (hub tick) + RTT_p50/2. Corroborates: loop lag max(W) > 50 ms, page hidden.
2. NETWORK. Decider: arrival lead, measured by the hub (RFC stream.arrival_lead: min per publish of start minus hub now at ingress; negative = arrived after its start). Threshold: arrival_lead_min(W) < schedule_latency while lead at send >= need. Phase 1 proxy (no hub change), marked "likely": uplink one-way delay from CLOCK sampled at 2 Hz while streaming, owd_up = t1 - t0 - offset_best; NETWORK if owd_up_max(W +- 0.5 s) > lead_send - need for the affected span, or a downlink gap >= max(3 x period, 100 ms) on the at-rate telemetry channel with loop lag < 50 ms.
3. HUB. Decider: arrived on time (arrival lead >= schedule_latency) and plan.late (RFC) incremented in W, or stream.starved with no late arrival. Corroborates: plan compute time against the react budget.
4. UNKNOWN: nothing decisive; evidence kept, said plainly.
The 10-08 case separates: a slow but connected link gives a clean lead at send and a negative arrival lead (or an owd_up spike plus a downlink gap) = NETWORK; the trace leak gives a falling lead at send plus loop lag = CLIENT; a slow solve gives a clean arrival plus plan.late = HUB.
Over WS there is no visible packet loss: TCP turns loss into delay, so "gaps" is the honest word. GRANT rate cuts are the hub's own congestion verdict.

== 4. Conditions (short line per COPY.md, then the detail sentence and one action, expanded under the row) ==
Format: id | signal: enter (hold) / clear (hold) | severity | short line | detail | action
LINK
L1 cutout-client | episode CLIENT | warn, act at >= 3 in 60 s | Motion paused: this device fell behind | This computer was too busy to send the next moves in time, so the machine stopped and waited. | Close other apps, or reload Phosphor
L2 cutout-network | episode NETWORK | warn, act at >= 3 in 60 s | Motion paused: WiFi delay | The moves left this device on time but reached the machine late, so it stopped and waited. | Move closer to the router, or set Stream buffer to 1000 ms
L3 cutout-hub | episode HUB | warn | Motion paused: machine fell behind | The moves arrived on time, but the machine took too long to plan them. | Lower smoothness or speed; send a report
L4 cutout-unknown | episode UNKNOWN | info | Motion paused: cause unknown | The machine stopped briefly and the cause could not be pinned down. | Send a report if it repeats
L5 send-margin | lead_send_min < H/4 for 5 s / >= H/3 for 10 s | info | Sending close to the deadline | Moves are leaving with little time to spare; a small hiccup will pause the machine. | Close other apps
L6 slow-link | RTT p50 > 50 ms or jitter (p95 - p50) > 30 ms for 10 s / < 30 and < 15 for 30 s | warn | Slow connection to the machine | Messages take longer than usual to reach the machine and come back. | Move closer to the router
L7 delay-spike | one RTT or owd_up sample > 4x median and > 100 ms | info, Log only | WiFi delay spike 240 ms | - | -
L8 updates-stalled | downlink gap >= 500 ms while live and the loop healthy / none for 30 s | warn | Machine updates stalled | The machine's position updates stopped arriving for a moment. | Check the WiFi
L9 backlog | ws.bufferedAmount > 0 for 2 s / 0 for 10 s | act | Connection jammed | This device has data waiting that the network is not taking. | Check the WiFi; Phosphor reconnects if it lasts
L10 throttled | unsolicited GRANT lowers a subscribed rate / restored | info | Machine reduced update rate | The machine is sending fewer updates because the connection is congested. | Disconnect other devices using the machine
L11 drops | >= 2 reconnects in 5 min / none for 10 min | warn | Connection keeps dropping | The link to the machine keeps breaking and reconnecting. | Move the machine or the router closer
L12 weak-signal | link.rssi < -75 dBm for 30 s (warn), < -82 (act) / > -72 for 60 s | warn/act | Machine WiFi signal weak | The machine hears the router faintly, which causes delays. | Move the router closer; keep the antenna clear of metal
L13 hub-wifi-drop | link.drops increments | warn | Machine WiFi dropped | The machine lost its WiFi connection and rejoined. | Check the router
THIS DEVICE
D1 busy | event-loop lag p95 (1 min) > 25 ms for 2 min (warn), > 100 ms (act) / < 15 ms for 2 min | warn/act | This device is busy | Phosphor is waiting on this computer; controls and motion may lag. | Close other apps
D2 freeze | one stall >= 250 ms (timer drift or long task) | info, Log only | This device froze 0.3 s | - | -
D3 slow-display | render fps < 30 for 30 s while visible / >= 45 for 30 s | info | Display running slow | The screen is updating less often than usual. | Close other apps
D4 growth | heap floor (min per minute) +8 MB per 5 min for 3 windows running, or lag p95 2x the session baseline for 5 min while the floor rises / reload | warn | Phosphor slows down over time | Something in Phosphor keeps using more memory and time the longer it runs. | Reload Phosphor, then send a report
D5 overloaded | PressureObserver('cpu') serious 30 s (warn) or critical 10 s (act) / nominal or fair 60 s | warn/act | This computer is overloaded | The computer's processor is near its limit. | Close other apps
D6 workers | live workers > baseline + 2 / back to baseline | warn | folds into D4 (same words)
D7 background | page hidden while streaming / visible | warn | Phosphor is in the background | Some systems slow down apps in the background, which can pause the machine. | Keep Phosphor in front while playing
MACHINE
M1 late-plans | plan.late > 6/min for 1 min / < 1/min for 2 min | warn | Machine planner running late | The machine sometimes finishes planning a move after it should have started. | Lower smoothness; send a report
M2 fault | any health.fault field nonzero / zero | act | <group>: <catalog label>, e.g. Motor power: inrush | The machine reports a fault and switched something off. | Open the machine's Hardware page
M3 hub-memory | hub heap falls > 20% over 30 min | warn | Machine memory running low | The machine's controller has less free memory than it started with. | Restart the machine when idle
M4 hot | telemetry.temp above its declared max - 10% (only where the catalog declares a max) | warn | Machine running hot | A part of the machine is close to its temperature limit. | Let it cool; check airflow
M5 log-drops | log_dropped increments | info | Machine skipped log lines | - | -
M6 restarted | boot_id changed | info | Machine restarted | The machine rebooted since the last connection. | -
CPU on this device: no CPU percentage exists in a webview; PressureObserver is the native signal (WebView2/Chromium), loop lag the proxy elsewhere. JS heap: performance.memory (Chromium); on WebKit platforms the card says "not measured here". Renderer RSS via the shell is deferred until heap proves insufficient.

== 5. Alerting ==
- Hysteresis: each condition enters after its hold and clears after its clear hold; a re-entry within 60 s of clearing reopens the same incident (count + 1), never a new one; warn escalates to act by rate only and de-escalates only after the clear hold.
- Status slot: act and warn only; below link fault, unattended, refusal, jog note, history msg and latch notices; act above the safety edge and virtual, warn below the edge. Minimum dwell 5 s. Click opens Health.
- Log: one local entry per incident at open (tag health, level warn/info), count and duration updated in place on close. Line format: "<what> <size> · <cause>", e.g. "Motion paused 0.4 s · WiFi delay"; the evidence (numbers, jargon allowed) expands underneath.
- Health page (Valence tier, beside Link): three cards, Link / This device / Machine, one fact per line, plain words first, the number right, "not reported by this machine" for a missing role; a 2-minute strip on the Link card (RTT, lead at send, arrival lead, cutout markers colored by cause); the incident list below with Send report. Each card is placeable on the Dash.
- Link card lines: status; round trip and jitter; sent ahead (min); arrived ahead (min, RFC); gaps in 2 min and the longest; backlog; frames per second each way (needs ph-cmz); machine signal (RSSI); machine WiFi drops; reconnects; update-rate cuts.
- This device card: responsiveness (lag p95); frame rate; memory and its 10-min trend; CPU pressure; workers; growth alarm line.
- Machine card: late plans per minute; plan time vs budget; faults; memory trend; temperatures; log drops; a link to the device's own diagnostic cards.

== 6. Local tracking (no telemetry) ==
- Health ring in memory: 1 Hz rows of every metric for 10 min, 10 Hz for the last 2 min of the stream signals (lead at send, owd, gaps); bounded, under 1 MB.
- Incident snapshot at open: the ring over [-60 s, +30 s] in time relative to the incident, the classification and evidence, the settings that matter (stream buffer, schedule latency, lookahead). Last 20 in memory; the last 5 also in localStorage (try/catch) so a reload, the D4 remedy, keeps them.
- Nothing leaves the device except through the reviewed report (child bead).

== 7. What needs a Valence RFC (one RFC, "Health roles", number at drafting via rfc-lifecycle) ==
- link.rssi: hub radio RSSI, i8 dBm, 0 = none (Nucleus field exists; tag only)
- link.drops: u32 station disconnects since boot (new counter in main.cpp's handler)
- stream.arrival_lead: i32 us, min per publish of start - hub now at ingress for the owning stream (onStreamBundle already computes it before clamping)
- stream.late: u32 samples that arrived after their start
- stream.starved: u32 times the stream ran out and the hub braked (the settle counter, tagged)
- plan.late: u32 re-plans that landed after the motion moved on (_late_plans, exists)
- health.fault: select or bitfield, nonzero = needs attention, label from the catalog (motor_fault now; the drive alarm when val-091.73 lands)
- telemetry.heap: u32 bytes, the hub's largest free block (memory-budget T21: maxblock decides, free does not)
Phosphor-only: everything measured on the client (lead at send and clips, CLOCK owd at 2 Hz while streaming, loop lag, heap, pressure, fps, backlog, reconnects, GRANT cuts, telemetry gaps, plan.* starvation), the classifier, the ring, the UI, the report flow.
Nucleus follow-ups (no RFC; for the val- board): log STA_DISCONNECTED with its reason plus a count; bridge esp_hosted/ESP_LOG warnings into geiger; RSSI in the 5 s liveness line; count past-due samples in onStreamBundle; make sync_seg_bundles and reset_gen honest; valencesim fault flags --plan-delay-ms N --plan-delay-every-s S.

== 8. Test plan ==
- Pure (test/health.test.mjs): classify(evidence) table; hysteresis state machine on a fake clock; growth detector on synthetic series; report bundle builder (allowlist, no forbidden fields, size).
- Client stall: Playwright + valencesim + funscript player; a 300 ms busy loop in the page mid-play -> CLIENT in the Log and on the card; page hidden -> D7.
- Network: Playwright's page.routeWebSocket (playwright ^1.62 is installed; no relay process or new dependency) delays c2h frames 300 ms for 2 s -> NETWORK (phase 1 via the owd proxy, phase 2 via arrival lead); hold every frame -> backlog and updates-stalled; close -> drops.
- Hub late: the valencesim plan-delay flag (Nucleus sim-only bead) -> plan.late -> HUB; until it exists the hub path is covered by the pure table.
- Report: covered by the child bead's acceptance.

== 9. Order ==
Phase 1, Phosphor-only and shippable: ph-cmz counters; door lead and clip stats; CLOCK 2 Hz while streaming; device sampler (lag, heap, pressure, fps, workers, visibility); ring; classifier (CLIENT decisive, NETWORK likely, HUB and UNKNOWN interim); Health page, slot and Log; the report flow (child bead).
Phase 2, after the RFC and the Nucleus counters: roles bound, NETWORK and HUB decisive, machine conditions M1-M3.
Remedy that exists today for network cutouts: the hub's schedule_horizon setting at 1000 ms gives the player a 500 ms lookahead (RFC-087); L2's action names it.

== 10. BLE sideband (assessment, for the record) ==
The hub has no BLE yet (CONFIG_BT_ENABLED unset; val-9u0.3 open). Under esp_hosted, BLE HCI shares the C6's one 2.4 GHz radio (time-sliced coexistence) and the same SDIO link as WiFi, so an SDIO or esp_hosted stall takes both down, and a held BLE connection costs WiFi airtime. The session layer is mostly ready (any frame is proof of life, per-channel stream seq drops duplicates, intent_id and estop_seq dedupe), the binding layer is not: one session has one transport, and RFC-046 makes a second HELLO a migration that closes the first. Smallest RFC: a sideband HELLO flag that joins a LIVE session as a second binding (never a migration), h2c limited to the never-shed set plus CLOCK/PONG, c2h anything (deduped), liveness from either binding. Recommendation: defer until this health system shows the cutouts are network and a 1000 ms stream buffer does not ride them out.

title: funscript player: the scheduler sends a different curve than it draws (knotSlope handoff cap, dwellMerge)
description: Found with the Kinetic² lab (Nucleus tools/kinetic-lab, val-b7m) on 2026-10-06: the built-in PCHIP sine (period 1300 ms, 100 ms knots, 0.3 amplitude, factory limits, window 0..500 mm) rendered through the board's own planner. Against the player's drawn curve the plan errs mean 1.8 mm, p95 7.2 mm, worst 18 mm at the script's end; with the author's knots sent as they are (the lab's exact sender) it errs mean 0.75 mm, and 0.215 mm once a 2 ms lead is removed, with the first span the only outlier (kin-tt8). The planner renders the author's cubic; the scheduler's wire differs from the drawn curve in two places. (1) scheduler.js knotSlope caps every end velocity at HANDOFF_K (1.5) times the lesser chord. PCHIP's slope (the MFP weighted harmonic mean) reaches 2 x the lesser chord, so near every extremum of a sampled sine the sent velocity is below the drawn slope (30 of 200 knots here; e.g. sent -371 mm/s where the curve's slope is -497 mm/s). The plan leaves those knots slower, then catches up: the concave-where-convex rise the operator saw on the bench. Kinetic² renders an end velocity literally (HandoffBounded is reserved: the solver owns junction velocities), so the cap no longer protects anything the hub does not already handle; registry segment_handoff_k 1.5 is the hub's SHOULD bound (RFC-049c), not a sender's duty. (2) scheduler.js dwellMerge drops a knot that moves on in the same direction by less than DWELL_SPAN (0.02 of the window, 10 mm on a 500 mm window) past the last kept knot. Near every extremum of a slow sine that merges a knot, and at the script's end the last 200 ms become one smoothstep span instead of two PCHIP spans: the 18 mm worst error. The hub's dwell rule tests the target against the previous ACCEPTED target on the same source; a monotone step smaller than the span is still a hold to it, so the merge is a real constraint, but it costs the drawn shape. Ruling needed (operator; data to firmware): (a) stop pre-capping end velocities for cubic modes whose slope is the mode's own (the hub bounds, Kinetic² renders), (b) make the drawn line the wire's line (shape() applying the same cap and merge) so what the operator sees is what is sent, or both. Either way the lab's exact sender is the reference.
close_reason: 2026-10-09 triage: superseded. The player rewrite sends every knot free and reversals at rest (cb132ea, 3b98576, ph-hcof) and retired the client curve surface (82f4b0e); knotSlope and dwellMerge no longer exist (grep of src, plugins, test). The hub renders what the twin draws.

title: Dash drag displaces: the dragged card lands where asked and pushes the cards it covers down
description: Ruling 2 (2026-10-06). Today grid.js place() lays the saved cards first and pushes the pin to the first free row below, so a card can only reach a spot through a gap. Displacement over an insertion target: place() is already a collide-and-push-down placer, so laying the pins first and pushing the covered cards is an order swap in one function; an insertion target needs a reading order the absolute grid does not have (only the stacked phone drag has one).
design: grid.js place(): pins first (a pin on an earlier pin still moves down, never overlaps), then every other card in reading order keeps its rect or moves to the first free row below; then only the cards that moved fall upward in reading order, x untouched (pack's last loop). commitPin writes every card whose drawn rect differs from its saved entry, so the commit equals the preview. The preview stays pure: each frame is computed from the saved map, so a card pushed by the pin returns when the pin moves on. Applies to every place(pin) caller: the pointer drag, the group drag and Align left/top/Spread; the keyboard nudge still picks a free rect (nudgePin); a resize still stops at a neighbor (blocker), never pushes. Nest drop (pin.into) and drag-out are untouched.
acceptance_criteria: 1. grid-model tests: a pin on a taken rect lands exactly where asked; the covered card moves to the first free row below it; a chain pushes on; nothing overlaps; untouched cards keep their rects; the dragged card's old slot stays a hole; commitPin after a preview reproduces the preview exactly (property test replaces 'no other card moves'). 2. A browser test drags a card onto another in edit mode: mid-drag the other card is drawn below the ghost; after release both commits hold across a reload; Escape mid-drag restores every card. 3. The DashGrid and grid.js header constraints that say 'the preview moves the dragged card only' are rewritten to the new rule. 4. npm run check zero findings.
close_reason: place() lays pins first and displaces the cards they cover; commitPin writes every moved card

1428x900 (launch size) · page frame · .app pads left/right by --gap (12 px) and .frame pulls itself out by -5 px to meet the hero panel's outline, so the bottom status row floats 12 px in from the window corners and the content column stops short of the right edge. Operator measured: .app 0 and .frame 0 fix it, footer meets the corners. Cause: the hero panel's og-panel outline (4 px offset + 1 px) was the thing the page aligned to; with the margin gone the content's inner right edge now needs the same 2 px edge treatment the left has (to confirm which: the rail's 2 px gap/grid). Rule candidate: one frame padding token on all four sides, chrome (strip, footer) full-bleed, the hero's outline inside the frame rather than the frame outside the outline (ph-p43h).
all widths · sidebar scroll recess (.rail [data-shade]) · (a) the shade stops short of the rail's corners: the rail has 6 px padding and a radius, the sticky ::before/::after sit inside the padding box so the gradient ends 6 px in and the rounded corner shows a gap; (b) the ink is rgba(0,0,0,.95) over --bg-raised, reads heavy: operator wants a tint (shade ink from the theme, e.g. --bg-sunken or the accent at low alpha, not pure black); (c) bottom edge flickers in the last few px when not scrolled to the end: the ::after carries margin-top -24 px inside a flex column with a 2 px gap, and scrollshade toggles data-shade-bottom at scrollHeight - 1 px, so sub-pixel scroll positions flip the attribute and the last row shifts by the gap. The trick itself works (operator: noticed it without noticing it). Rule candidate: shades drawn by the scroller's own overlay element that covers padding and radius (inset 0 of the scroller, clip-path to the radius), ink = theme token, hysteresis of 2 px on the toggle (ph-p43h / ph-acnj).
1428x900 · hero rail (HeroStrip: numeral + planned target/lag/speed + plan strip with position bar and ruler) · takes roughly a third of the window height at the launch size and a larger share as the window shrinks; it is a fixed-height stack with no budget relative to the viewport. Over widths: the share grows as height shrinks because the rail never gives anything up. Rule candidate for 10.12: the hero has a height budget per bucket (a fraction of the viewport with a floor), the numeral scales within the budget (HeroNumerals already derives font-size from --num-h), and the plan strip's two rows (bar, ruler) become one row under the budget; the strip's e-stop/pause pair never moves (RENDERING row 11).
1428x900 · category pages (Motion: Limits / Settings on trial / Ceiling overrides) · every card lays itself out by a different rule: LimitsWidget is a role composite with its own repeat(auto-fit, minmax(220px,1fr)) grid and two bright sub-group titles inside the card (88 px row pitch, columns fill the width); the trial list is a chip list; the Ceiling overrides card is plain fields placed in cell-quantized columns, so the last ~116 px of card width is an empty gutter and its rows are 55 px; the page's '3 advanced / Reset' row sits outside any card 4 px left of the card edge; column gaps 15 vs 12 px. Same pattern in AdvancedGeneratorWidget and PatternWidget (each a private auto-fit grid). Rule candidate: ONE card-body layout for fields and composites alike: columns come from the bucket (cell-quantized), the row's remainder stretches so no card ends in a gutter, one row height per presentation (ph-z50z rungs), sub-group titles and section headers are one type step each and nowhere else, composites may not carry a private grid rule (ph-acnj lint catches grid-template-columns in src/ui/hero and plugins). Page-level actions (advanced toggle, Reset) move with ph-lxea's head controls.

title: Trial write refused: UNSUPPORTED_OP (Chase dense ms) on the 0.1.9 P4 bench hub from the analyzer/Tuning preview; find whether the hub lacks the RFC-099 trial op for that field or the client sends the wrong op; fix the right side
notes:
Diagnosis 2026-10-07: the hub refuses on purpose. ValenceDevice::trialBaseline (c89ae84) excludes 0x3120 key 10 chase_dense_ms because a live samples grant commits to it (applyTuning), so a trial that a revert would undo cannot be honored; the library then NACKs UNSUPPORTED_OP. Nothing on the wire tells a client: 0x0016 is declared, the trial_mask bit for chase_dense_ms exists (never set), and RFC-099 has no per-key refusal rule. Fix on both sides: Valence RFC-107 draft (a hub MAY refuse a trial write per key with UNSUPPORTED_OP and a detail naming why; the client falls back to a durable write) and Phosphor's Tuning preview treating UNSUPPORTED_OP on a trial write as not trialable for the session, offering the durable write instead. Hub side unchanged.
Correction 2026-10-07 (RFC-107 drafter): SPEC 9.3 item 5 already permits a per-key UNSUPPORTED_OP for a value the hub gates on live machine state, so the hub was conformant; what was missing is the surround (a detail naming the key and why, the fixed-while-etag-holds rule, the client fallback duty), now RFC-107 (Valence 8d1b35f, molecule rfc-mol-n3t at review). Also: the durable write of chase_dense_ms is itself refused INTERLOCK while a samples grant is live, so the client fallback may be refused too; that is the key's ordinary rule.
2026-10-08 F1 from the RFC-107 review fixed: after a refused trial the preview no longer sends a durable write (write() confirms only destructive fields, so chase_dense_ms would have reached flash with no operator action). writeTrial on a marked key now returns ok:false 'not trialable here, write it from the settings page' and sends nothing; the operator writes the key from the settings page. Test (f) and PLUGINS.md say so.
close_reason: Hub refuses a trial of chase_dense_ms on purpose (a live samples grant commits to it, UNSUPPORTED_OP); client rule: a trial NACKed UNSUPPORTED_OP marks channel:key not trialable for the session, no retry, the next write goes durable behind the host confirm (Valence RFC-107 draft).

title: Fixed-height strip, compact top bar, rail swaps to the plan strip during motion
description:
Operator feedback 2026-10-02 (three annotated screenshots against valencesim). Build exactly:
1. NO PAGE SHIFTING. Top bar and strip fixed height. Errors, NACK refusals and the safety notice render in ONE status slot in the strip's center, overwriting by priority with a text reason; never a new line. The Pause-cleared banner line and the separate global refusal row are deleted.
2. ONE compact top bar, one row: left the heatmap mark and hub name; right the chips, then the window buttons (shell only). One live indicator (the phase chip); the second "live", the WS chip, the Menu handle and the shell row go. The bar is the Tauri drag region.
3. THE STRIP is the hero row: numerals left (hero, target, lag, speed); right one group: Halt-or-E-Stop and Pause (SafetyOp), Override/Return, Home (Force Home). Safety-reach holds at every viewport.
4. THE RAIL ROW under the strip, fixed height: the jog tape, replaced in place by PlanStrip while a source owns the rail (control-owner plus the pattern running role); swaps back on release.
5. Shell shading on the top bar (and, via ph-e82.16, the sidebar's Phosphor section); not on the strip or rail.

FINER CHOICES (each veto-able; record a ruling here to change one):
V1 Status slot priority: link fault > unattended > refusal > latch notice (halted / override / paused) > latest safety edge > idle (empty). Unattended outranks a refusal because RENDERING 10.1 rule 3 says moving-with-nobody-attached MUST be visible.
V2 The "no hub link" and "Link error" banners (LinkBar) moved into the slot as the fault class.
V3 A refusal stays until its remedy echoes OR the operator dismisses it with an x in the slot (new); it keys on lastRefusal.at, so a timeout fault with no NACK code now shows too.
V4 The numerals are rendered by TopStrip from RailWidget's published readout (getters over the rail's rAF state), so numeral and comet still share one instant. With no rail mounted the numeral area is empty and the strip keeps its height.
V5 Strip height depends on the viewport only: max(numeral block, --tap) + 12 px on one row at >= 760 px; at < 760 px two fixed rows (numerals + status, then the controls). Secondary numerals that do not fit wrap below and clip rather than grow the strip.
V6 Override/Return shows only while a rail is mounted (law 7, axis archetype); Home, Force Home and any other action.home / action.safety op render as one scrolling row after the pair; the e-stop/pause pair never scrolls.
V7 Flip stays on the rail: it rides the right end of the rail row.
V8 The jog tape's disabled reason renders inside its own label line ("jog . window . paused: press Override to jog"), not as a line under it; the inline "jog refused" echo is dropped (the slot shows the refusal).
V9 Rail owned = pattern running OR any control-owner slot held by a session other than this one; override latched shows the tape again (override is the one way to take the rail). A stream from this same session reads as unowned (ponytail, per-source once source ids are registry vocabulary).
V10 PlanStrip no longer collapses: inside the swap it always shows, dimming its lane when no plan is streaming.
V11 The two link dots and the decorative crosshair are deleted; the phase chip is the one live indicator, the rx chip carries telemetry health.
V12 The drag region is the top bar only (was the whole strip).
V13 TransportBar renders nothing (Home moved to the strip); App.svelte's three mounts are the sibling's to drop, then the file is deleted.
acceptance_criteria: safety-reach and responsive-matrix pass at every viewport; shell-chrome-geometry asserts bar height constant with and without a refusal, strip height constant with a long hub name and a long reason, rail row height constant across the swap; npm run check zero, npm test, npm run test:browser pass; Playwright against valencesim shows the swap and the refusal slot.
notes:
More finer choices (veto-able):
V14 Phone (< 760 px): two fixed grid rows, the primary numeral beside the status slot, the controls under them (a wrapping flex row once pushed the pair to a clipped third line; the grid makes that impossible). Watch size (<= 300 px): a current condition (fault, unattended, refusal, notice) covers the numeral cell; the edge history is left to the Log there.
V15 One-row shrink order: extra ops (Force Home, Clear Override, other device ops) scroll first, then the secondary numerals clip, then Override and Home scroll; the pair never shrinks. At >= 1440 px the numerals never shrink. The status slot reserves min(240 px, 25%) even idle, so nothing moves when it fills.
V16 The refusal's text is its own dismiss button (with an x glyph), beside "Fix: <op>" when the hub advertises the remedy; the refusal shows as "refused: CODE (label)", the detail in its title.
V17 The fault slot carries "Retry now" while the link is retrying or failed, so App's HubPicker mode=link row (which shifts the page ~50 px when the link drops) can go (sibling's call, comment on ph-e82.16).
V18 Bar: phase and tier chips are pinned; hub, catalog, render, rx shed first, then the name ellipsizes; under 400 px the heatmap (decor) goes first. Window buttons 40 px wide under 480 px. The rule under the bar is an inset shadow so the window buttons get the full bar height. Shell chip labels lift to --tx-val for 4.5:1.
V19 Close gate (operator request 2026-10-02): the X and every OS close request (onCloseRequested, preventDefault) open one popover under the X, out of flow (RENDERING 9 overlay), "Close Phosphor?" plus live consequences: background-run pattern keeps running > this session owns a source and it settles > the buttplug server is running (bp_status at open). One input: a 1 s press-and-hold (pointer or Enter/Space), intent-blue fill, never red; Esc or a click outside cancels and returns focus to the X. The hold destroys the window (close() would only re-raise the request), so src-tauri/capabilities/default.json gains core:window:allow-destroy (cargo check clean). With no event permission the gate degrades: the X still asks, an OS close goes through.
V20 Clipped chrome text must carry its full form in a title: the responsive matrix's clip check now skips text whose own or ancestor title contains it (the wordmark, the slot texts).

OWED: by-hand Tauri check of the close gate (X, Alt+F4, taskbar close, hold on a touch screen) and of the bar as the drag region; agents may not launch the window.

comments.author: AtlanticTM
comments.text:
2026-10-02 VETO-ABLE DECISIONS (ph-e82.15, recorded per the autonomy bar):

1. Edit toggle: ONE button, "Edit layout" / "Done" (aria-pressed), at the bar's right end. The layout picker is ALWAYS shown (switching layouts is a view choice, not an edit), so the active layout's name is on screen in and out of edit mode. Edit mode adds the cell lattice behind the grid and a one-line hint (grip moves, corner resizes, palette entries drag; arrows move, Shift+arrows resize; Ctrl+Z undoes). Handles stay edit-mode only (the rule stands).
2. Law 12: grab and resize handles are max(40 CSS px, --tap) at every scale step (at scale 0.67, --tap alone is 33 px). Asserted in responsive-matrix at 1280 and 0.67.
3. Drop target: a dashed intent-colored outline over the cells where the card lands, for pointer move/resize and palette drags. Not drawn when stacked (phone width keeps its live reorder). An empty grid keeps three cell rows in edit mode so it can take a drop.
4. Undo: ONE level over the whole layouts store (placements, nests, looks, layout save/rename/delete, module delete). Each synchronous burst of edits is one step (a palette add with a look is one step), recorded only if the store actually changed (a click on a grip never costs the real last change). Not undoable: layout switch, scale. Undo button plus Ctrl+Z / Cmd+Z in edit mode unless a text control has focus.
5. Palette: sections stay collapsed until searched (as before); search also matches section and presentation names. Each field entry lists its offered presentations as chips (derived first); a chip adds the field with that look. An unplaced, placeable entry drags onto the grid (lands at the drop cell, fills to the row's end, at least 8 cells) or onto a nest (joins it unplaced, flows at its end). HTML5 drag: on touch, click-to-add stays the path.
6. Safety ops are TOP LEVEL ONLY (grid.js placeable('safety', inNest) false): a scrolling nest could carry a stop out of view (law 11), and the strip's copy is the one that cannot go. The palette tags them "Also in the strip" (red, --bad), "Strip and top level only" when a nest is the target, with Add disabled and the entry not draggable. Flip: drop 'safety' from placeable's first line.
7. Toolbar: [scale - % +] [layout picker] ... [Undo] [New nest] [Layout...] [Edit layout/Done]. Save as, Rename, Delete, Reset layout and the module picker (Insert, Delete module) live in ONE popover menu: top layer (never clipped, never widens the page), anchored to its button by CSS anchor positioning, flipping above or inward when there is no room; without anchor support it opens centered (UA default). One row at 1280 and 1920; two rows on a phone, no horizontal scroll, menu on screen (all asserted in responsive-matrix). Reset layout moved into the menu: it is destructive and rare (undo covers it now).
8. Default card width: an item nobody sized FILLS THE ROW at any DPR (was 48 cells: 864 CSS px on a DPR 2 1440 window, 60 percent of it). Reasons: the old 12-span model's full span was always the whole pane, and ph-e82.5 decision 8 already said added modules land full width. A migrated full-span (12) card is stored with no w, so it fills the row at any DPR too; partial spans keep 4 cells per span (proportional would need cols at load time). Cost: a 4K window no longer tiles two unsized cards side by side. Alternative if vetoed: N-up tiling by CSS width (n = floor(grid width / ~1200 px)), which needs cell CSS px threaded into pack.
9. An entry with no position yet (a look set before the item is placed, a reset nest) flows as unsaved at its own size, keeping its look (grid.js pack).
10. ph-e82.10 verified holding with the toolbar changes: the matrix home scenario's announce-region containment passes at 1280 and 1920, nest.test's first-nest draw on a view with no map passes.
11. ph-vdk.40: fixed in owned files (chart legend, custom theme swatch, dash card titles); minWidth stays 320 (details on ph-vdk.40).
12. ph-6i9: fixed in shadow.svelte.js (per-write stamp); the drain sleep in test/control-contract.test.mjs (not this agent's file) can go (details on ph-6i9).

Steps: (1) shell tokens --shell-bg/--shell-fg/--shell-border in style.css, applied to the shell row and drawer only; (2) src/shell/Drawer.svelte dropping from the shell row, panes Hubs (discovery + transport moved out of the row), Server (ServerPane as-is), Settings (registered via src/shell/drawer.js registerDrawerPane), About (hub identity, versions, UI build); row keeps handle, link state, window buttons; Escape and click outside close; in flow so it pushes the strip's safety pair down, never covers it (RENDERING 9, laws 1/11); open + pane remembered in localStorage; (3) phone width: full width, scrolls within itself, page scroll never trapped; (4) shell-chrome-geometry + responsive matrix + a11y. TEST/VALIDATION PLAN: npm run check zero, npm test, npm run test:browser; the geometry test builds the real shell bundle with a stubbed Tauri runtime and asserts the e-stop stays on screen with the drawer open at desktop and phone sizes.
acceptance_criteria: Drawer opens from the shell row; e-stop and pause visible and clickable with it open at 1440x900, 420x800 and a landscape phone; shell chrome visibly darker than content in default, light-ish themes and hi-vis with a11y contrast passing; npm run check, npm test, npm run test:browser all pass.
notes:
VETO-ABLE DECISIONS (2026-10-02, agent):
1. Shading: --shell-bg = color-mix(--bg-sunken 40%, #000), --shell-fg = --ink, --shell-border = --line-3. PUSHBACK: the frozen chassis is already near black (--bg #08090B), so 'darker' has ~3% luminance headroom; the --line-3 rule under the shell carries most of the visible boundary. Lifting content surfaces instead would break the frozen-chassis rule. Measured: shell lum 0.0006 vs content 0.0027/0.0047; shell text worst 7.27:1 (default, hi-vis, prefers-contrast).
2. Desktop (>=960): the drawer is IN FLOW between the shell row and the LinkBar, so it pushes the e-stop/pause pair DOWN (operator's wording). max-height min(40dvh, 480px), scrolls within itself.
3. Phone (<960): the drawer opens BELOW THE WHOLE STRIP, over the content (position absolute in the sticky strip), so the e-stop never moves on a phone. Reason: in flow, the sticky strip grew past half a 568px screen and content under it failed the reach check. Content under the open drawer is covered by design; one --tap band stays uncovered to tap out.
4. Close on click, never pointerdown: closing moves the pair on desktop, and a control that moves between press and release loses the click (or the 3 s release hold). Tested: an e-stop click with the drawer open reaches the e-stop, then closes the drawer.
5. First run (no shell_drawer key and no shell_host) opens the drawer on Hubs, since discovery is the front door. Keys: shell_drawer ('1'/'0'), shell_drawer_pane.
6. Row keeps: Menu handle, WS/BLE chip, link phase, window buttons. The old collapse toggle is gone. Discovery, BLE scan, host entry (now with recent hubs, non-dense), the WS-upgrade button, notes and BLE wire counters moved to Hubs.
7. registerDrawerPane({id,label,component}) in src/shell/drawer.js (svelte/store writable, so late registration works): a built-in id (hubs/server/settings/about) replaces that pane; any other id adds a tab before About. Settings shows 'Nothing here yet.' until registered (settings-pane.js already registers id settings).
8. About: hub title (live identity.name, else WELCOME hub_name, else product), product, firmware, dialed endpoint, shell version (getVersion, '--' if denied), UI build.
9. Tabs follow WAI-ARIA: roving tabindex, ArrowLeft/Right, Home/End.
10. Shell window buttons and handle go to 40px under pointer: coarse (law 12).

title: RFC-085: override/return as one control on the rail's control row; jog replaces user in roles and labels
description:
RFC-085 (Valence rfc-crn), operator rulings 2026-10-01 (comments 00:29 jog vocabulary, 00:39 mode merge, 00:42 final naming).

Change:
- override/return is an ESSENTIAL BINDING of the axis archetype: one two-state control on the rail widget's control row (beside home and Flip). Press = override (latches pause, hands the rail to the operator, lifts limits, enables jog); second press = return (smooth return to the paused position, then plain pause; no gate). A client with no rail control declines it and renders nothing (law 7); it is not a free-standing safety module. bypass and override_on/off controls retire; the per-move bypass key is not sent (follow the landed text).
- Jog (tap-to-move) is offered only under override; outside override a jog is refused by the hub (SOURCE_CONFLICT) while a source owns the rail, and the rail shows that refusal. Window edits stay live at all times.
- 'jog' replaces 'user' in roles and labels: src/model/roles.js limitUserSpeed/limitUserAccel ('limit.user.speed'/'limit.user.accel') follow the landed registry names; any UI copy saying user speed.

Likely files: src/ui/hero/RailWidget.svelte, src/model/roles.js, src/model/actions.js (HAZARD_SAFETY_OPS override_on/bypass_on), src/ui/TransportBar.svelte, docs/DESIGN.md. Consumes Valence rfc-q93.

Prove it: unit test: rail declines override/return when the role is absent, binds when present; live smoke against valencesim: tap-to-move under a stream refused, override then jog accepted outside limits, return lands at the paused position; npm run check zero findings.
close_reason: Device-free complete (see the 2026-10-02 comment for commit, decisions, verification); live checks owed on ph-vdk.55

comments.author: AtlanticTM
comments.text:
2026-10-02 landed in 0f6f56f (roles rename in 4b5f99f). Decisions (VETO-ABLE):

1. Override/Return is SafetyOp with op = override, rendered in RailWidget's hero row (.rw-hero-accessory) before Flip and the Home accessory. No rail, no control; a hub whose safety-intents op table lacks override, no control (law 7).
2. Override is confirm-gated (actions.js HAZARD_SAFETY_OPS = {override}: it lifts the window and soft limits); Return takes no gate (law 14). Confirm copy is client text describing SPEC §11.1.
3. PUSHBACK, flagged: the task text said "jog enabled only while override is latched". Landed SPEC §11.4 (RFC-085 open question 2, answered at landing) says a manual point move on an idle, unpaused, unowned rail is an ordinary source activation, so gating the tape to override-only would take away a move the hub accepts. Coded the hub's gate instead: e-stop latched -> disabled "e-stop latched: no motion until release"; paused without override -> disabled "paused: press Override to jog" (hub: INTERLOCK); override -> enabled over the whole travel ("jog · travel"); idle and unpaused -> enabled over the window. A source owning the rail is the hub's SOURCE_CONFLICT, shown as "jog refused: SOURCE_CONFLICT (a source owns the rail: press Override to jog)". Veto to make it override-only and I flip one derived.
4. Jog naming: limit.jog.speed/accel (Jog speed/accel), the Limits widget's "Jog limits", the tape's mode label and aria-label. The tape's CSS class names are unchanged (probes key on them). No per-move bypass key was ever sent from the rail.

Verified device-free: check:safety ALL PASS (decline with no rail and with an op table cut before override, rail still present in the latter; one control beside Home; paused reason; confirm with nothing sent before it; Override -> Return -> Override on the wire as 7, 8; tape domain switches to travel); npm run check zero, npm test green.

title: RFC-085: TCode and buttplug adapters RESUME explicitly; no motion intent clears pause
description:
RFC-085 (Valence rfc-crn) description item 4 and ruling 2026-10-01: Phosphor's TCode and buttplug adapters RESUME EXPLICITLY. Under the fold no motion intent clears PAUSE (RESUME is the only clear; RFC-074 under RFC-085 drops stream bundles while paused and counts them).

Change: the adapters (src/model/motion.js TCode path, src/plugins/buttplug.js, src/shell/bp-server.js) never assume a motion intent or a STREAM bundle re-arms the machine. When paused, incoming motion is refused locally with a visible 'machine paused' reason (no silent drops), and resume is an explicit act (the strip control, or an adapter command the operator maps), sent as RESUME; StopCmd/stopAll keep their current meaning for toys and map to PAUSE for the machine only if the ruling's adapter text says so (state the choice here). The bp-server 'stop sends nothing' comment and buttplug.js header are rewritten to the new model.

Prove it: test/buttplug-bridge.test.mjs and a TCode adapter test: motion while paused is refused with a reason and nothing reaches the wire; after RESUME motion flows; test/buttplug-estop-sim.mjs still passes.
close_reason: Device-free complete (see the 2026-10-02 comment for commit, decisions, verification); live checks owed on ph-vdk.55

One guard where every adapter routes: motion.js createMotionDoor takes an optional halted() dep; shadow.svelte.js wires it to the REPORTED latch (machine.safety): "paused, resume to continue", or "e-stop latched, release and resume to continue". While it returns a reason every input is refused with it and nothing is published or set. This is a mirror of the hub's latch, not a second policy: the hub still drops (and counts) the bundles itself.
2. Neither adapter, nor the door, has a resume path. Resume is only the operator's strip Resume. No plugin API addition for an adapter-mapped resume (RFC-085's "send resume explicitly" read as: only an explicit operator act sends it).

title: RFC-085: top strip pair becomes pause/resume and estop/release, one control each; hold-to-release; Halt label when estop_cuts_power is false
description:
RFC-085 (Valence rfc-crn), operator rulings 2026-10-01 (comments 00:42 final naming and control shape, 00:47 ESTOP behavior, 00:48 machines without a motor switch, 00:49 declaration duty).

Change (RENDERING law 1 follows):
- The persistent strip's mandatory pair is e-stop plus pause. EACH PAIR IS ONE CONTROL WITH TWO STATES: no separate clear/release/resume button anywhere. STOP and HOLD buttons and every clear button retire.
- Pause: press latches PAUSE (any tier, role-exempt), second press is RESUME (no gate).
- E-stop: press latches; the latched state reads 'Halted'; release is PRESS-AND-HOLD on the same control, 3 s (RENDERING SHOULD, every renderer class), so two panic taps never latch-then-release; the hub still answers CLEAR_REFUSED and the strip shows it. After release on a power-cutting hub the strip shows paused + home required (resume refused while unhomed).
- Label: a hub that declared estop_cuts_power TRUE renders 'E-Stop'; FALSE or ABSENT renders 'Halt' (Clients MUST NOT render E-Stop on a hub that declared false; absent = false).
- Refusal mapping (shadow.svelte.js NACK.ESTOP_ACTIVE -> estop_clear) follows the release rename.

Likely files: src/ui/TopStrip.svelte, src/ui/TransportBar.svelte, src/model/actions.js (HAZARD_SAFETY_OPS), src/model/shadow.svelte.js, src/model/machine.svelte.js (safety word decode, one PAUSE bit), docs/DESIGN.md strip section. Coordinates with ph-e82.2 (strip in progress). Consumes Valence rfc-q93 at the pin bump.

Prove it: test/safety-reach.test.mjs and responsive-matrix assert exactly one e-stop and one pause control in the strip at every viewport; a fixture with estop_cuts_power false asserts the label is 'Halt' (H1 made testable, named by the 00:48 ruling); a fixture with it absent asserts 'Halt'; a hold shorter than 3 s sends nothing; live smoke against valencesim: pause, resume, estop, hold-release.
close_reason: Device-free complete (see the 2026-10-02 comment for commit, decisions, verification); live checks owed on ph-vdk.55

title: controlKey gives uid keys for role fields in the running app (proxy identity)
description: settings.js controlKey() picks the role key only when byRole.get(role)[0] === f. In the app, machine is deep $state, so model.fields[i] reaches placeableControls as a Svelte proxy while model.byRole (a Map, never proxied) holds the raw object: the identity check always fails and every role field is keyed uid:<ch>:<name> (live valencesim: uid:4608:running for pattern.running). Node tests (settings-model) see raw objects and pass, so the suite cannot catch it. Law 10 prefers the role key; persisted home and nest keys are being written as uids today. Fix: compare uids (first[0].uid === f.uid) in controlKey, plus a test that keys the model through $state or compares against byRole by uid. test/home.test.mjs normalizes keys to uids (keyUid) and needs no change after the fix. Saved layouts already holding uid keys for role fields will go inert on the fix unless the lookup accepts both; decide before fixing.

title: ActionField payload inputs ignore the secret flag: a passphrase payload renders in plain text
description:
RFC-009.4 / SPEC §8.8 'Secrets (normative)': a secret-flagged field's value is never shown. Field.svelte honors flagBits.secret (WIDGET.secret, type=password), but src/ui/ActionField.svelte renders every tstr payload input as type=text, and settings.js pass 2 drops flagBits when it builds an action's payload list. A wifi_join passphrase typed into an action is therefore on screen in clear text. Found by the provisioning wizard agent.

title: Builder (d): home page replaces Overview; palette and edit mode
description:
Phase (d), DESIGN §10.1. The home page replaces Overview (App.svelte tab {id: 'machine', label: 'Overview'} and machineItems). Everything that lived only on Overview becomes a module (hero-rank leftovers, telemetry, card-zone heroes, loose actions) or is deleted with C-9 proof. Default home when the user has none: seeded from rank (RENDERING §4 hero surfaced, ph-vdk.36) plus the migrated Default layout from (b). Edit mode: a palette listing every placeable control (fields by category, composites, plugin widgets, safety modules); place, move, resize, delete; outside edit mode nothing is draggable (the DashItem grab-handle rule stands). Derived category pages stay and keep every field reachable (§12). Full class only until the mobile ruling (f).

TEST/VALIDATION PLAN:
- Playwright on the fake-hub harness: no Overview tab; every field Overview showed is reachable from home or its category page (diff against a list captured from the tree before the change); the palette lists every fixture-catalog field exactly once plus every claimed composite; edit mode toggles drag handles; a write in flight survives entering and leaving edit mode.
- test/responsive-matrix.mjs visits home instead of Overview; no regressions in overflow, clip, chrome, reach.
- test/safety-reach.test.mjs: deleting every placed module still leaves the strip e-stop.
- Live against valencesim: build a home from the palette, reload, it restores; against a sparser profile (when valencesim offers one) the same layout degrades with absent items inert, no throw.

Proven by test/home.test.mjs against test/fixtures/overview-before.json (captured from Overview before the change), full and handheld, drill-ins included.

To keep that true, Overview-only content moved INTO the derived tree: card-zone heroes (Pattern, Limits) render as cards at the top of the category page their claimed fields came from (a hero with no categorized field lands on the other page); uncategorized loose actions join the `other` overflow page (RENDERING §3), synthesized as an "Other" tab when the catalog has no other category.

title: Builder (b): physical-pixel square grid, scale control, named layouts store, migration of per-class dash layouts
description:
Phase (b), DESIGN §10.5 and §10.6 (layouts half). Replace the 12-column span model (dashboard.svelte.js DEFAULT_SPAN/MAX_SPAN, DashItem.svelte colPx) with square cells sized in device pixels: cell edge in CSS px = device px / devicePixelRatio, default in the 32 to 40 device px band measured at 3840x2160 at 125 percent. Cell count follows the window. A browser-style scale control multiplies the cell edge. Items carry {x, y, w, h} in cells. Scale is done by cell size and tokens, never CSS zoom on a subtree holding a positional control, until a test proves RailWidget's clientX mapping survives (ph-gf8's concern). Under a coarse pointer the scale clamps so no hit target drops under the 40 CSS px floor (law 12). Layout store: named layouts, per client, localStorage with the existing try/catch degrade; keyed on stable ids (law 10); absent ids stay inert. Migration: today's phosphor.dash.<cls>.<viewId> maps and the legacy sd32.dash.* keys seed a layout named Default; legacy keys are read, never written or deleted. rclass.js class selection stays in CSS px, unaffected.

TEST/VALIDATION PLAN (all device-free):
- New node suite test/grid-model.test.mjs (added to npm run check): device-px to CSS-px conversion at DPR 1, 1.25, 1.5, 2; cell count per window width; scale clamp under coarse pointer; save, rename, delete, switch named layouts; absent ids stay inert and survive a round trip; storage throwing degrades to in-memory; migration from a seeded 12-span map and from a legacy sd32 key keeps visual order and never writes the legacy key.
- test/dash-measure.test.mjs extended: measured cell edge in device px equals the target at deviceScaleFactor 1.25 and 2.
- test/responsive-matrix.mjs: no horizontal page scroll at any scale step; target floor holds at the smallest scale on phone viewports.
acceptance_criteria: DashGrid places {x,y,w,h} items on device-px square cells with a scale control; named layouts save, switch and survive reload; existing layouts migrate to Default with order kept; grid-model suite in npm run check.

comments.author: AtlanticTM
comments.text:
2026-10-01 decisions (veto-able, recorded per autonomy bar):
1. Scale is browser-style for the whole client: the step sets the --s token on <html> (rem, --tap, thumbs) and multiplies the cell edge. No CSS zoom anywhere (ph-gf8 RailWidget concern untouched).
2. Coarse pointer: scale never goes below 1. A --tap-derived floor (0.9 allowed) was tried and the matrix failed: chip-num inputs are rem-sized at ~42 CSS px and drop to 38 at 0.9. Floor proven at 1 only.
3. Max scale per window: a step is offered only while viewport/scale >= 320 CSS px (the narrowest laid-out viewport). 360 px phone gets 1 and 1.1.
4. Default card width 48 cells = 12 old spans x 4 (a full 1920 DPR1 pane); migration maps span s to 4s cells. Consequence: on DPR 2 (retina 1440) a default card is 864 CSS px, not full width; at 3840x2160@125% two cards sit side by side. Alternative if vetoed: unsaved items fill the row.
5. Rows are minmax(cell, auto): h is a floor; a card whose content is taller grows its rows, never clips a control. Items stretch to fill their area so a resize in cells is visible.
6. Vertical compaction: saved items keep their column and rise to the first free row; a drag pins the dragged item and everything else yields. Keyboard: Up/Down swap reading order, Left/Right step one cell, Shift+arrows resize.
7. Viewports <= 640 CSS px stack full width as before (mobile is ph-e82.7); a stacked drag commits a reading order, never cells.
8. Store: localStorage phosphor.layouts = {active, layouts: {name: {'<cls>.<viewId>': {id: {x,y,w,h}}}}}; one map per (renderer class, view) inside each named layout. phosphor.scale holds the wished step. phosphor.dash.* and sd32.dash.* are read to seed Default and never written or deleted; the store is written only on a user change.
9. Layout UI is minimal and lives in DashGrid's edit-mode toolbar (select, name field, Save as, Rename, Delete); the scale control (- 100% +) is always shown. ph-e82.5 owns the real palette and edit mode.

title: Builder (c): control contract: field + presentation registry from archetypes, resize and aspect orientation, composites and plugin widgets under it
description:
Phase (c), DESIGN §10.2. A control is one catalog field plus a presentation chosen from the set its archetype allows. Presentation registry keyed by archetype code, grown from settings.js resolveArchetype/resolveWidget and WIDGET; rendered by Field.svelte. The offered set is filtered by the field's facts: bar needs bounds, toggle and bulb need a bool, graph needs a client-side history ring (missing samples are gaps, law 9). The user picks how it looks, never what it binds (laws 6, 7). Every presentation keeps the universal contract: four-state ladder with text reason (law 5), graying with the gate named (law 3), stale dim (law 8), echo pair co-located and range pairs as one control (§11, mergeRangePairs). Resize: each control declares minimum cells per orientation; orientation follows its own aspect (w >= h horizontal). Role-claiming composites (heroes.js rail, pattern, limits; PlanStrip stays nested in the rail per §10 plan-view) are controls under the same placement, size and save rules; claimAll (roles.js) claim-or-decline is unchanged. Plugin heroes (host.js registerHero, zone card) become placeable controls under the same contract. Safety ops become placeable modules; the strip's mandatory e-stop is not one of them. Absorbs ph-vdk.22's placement question (a tuning composite is one more role-claiming control).

TEST/VALIDATION PLAN:
- test/settings-model.test.mjs: for every field in the fixture catalog, the offered presentation set is non-empty, contains the derived default, and never offers bar without bounds or toggle for a non-bool.
- test/plugins.test.mjs: a plugin hero is placeable, resizable and persisted under hero:plugin:<name>:<id>; a throwing plugin hero drops to generic fields as today.
- New Playwright suite test/control-contract.test.mjs on the fake-hub harness (responsive-matrix.mjs pattern): each presentation of one writable field shows pending then confirmed on a synthetic echo, overdue past the timeout, fault on a NACK, with the text reason; an aspect flip at w = h swaps orientation without dropping an in-flight write.
- Live against valencesim (test/actions-live.test.mjs pattern): one slider-class field driven through knob, slider and stepper, each confirmed on a second raw session (C-8).
- npm run check (device-knowledge gate) stays green.
acceptance_criteria: Every catalog field is placeable with a presentation from its allowed set; composites and plugin heroes place, resize and persist the same way; every presentation passes the four-state ladder suite; one field verified live on valencesim in three presentations.

comments.text:
2026-10-01 VETO-ABLE DECISIONS (orchestrator direction, recorded so the ph-e82.1 rulings can flip them):
(1) ph-e82.1 item 2, cross-archetype presentation: CODED CONSERVATIVE. settings.js offeredPresentations() offers only the derived archetype's projections (PRESENTATIONS keyed by UI_ARCHETYPE code: slider->slider,knob; stepper->stepper,knob; readout->readout,bar,numeral; chart->graph,readout,numeral; select->segmented,select; toggle->toggle,bitfield; text->text,secret). Flip: settings.js CROSS_ARCHETYPE = true gives the RFC-080 draft item 3 read/write-class rule (any writable presentation for a writable field, plus display-only read-only presentations). Reason: RFC-080 is DRAFT (rfc-94c); never code against an unaccepted clause. (2) ph-e82.1 item 3, law-10 keys: ACCEPTED uid keys for single fields with no role (controlKey: 'role:<role>' for a role's first-authored field, else 'uid:<channel id>:<field name>'; range pairs join both keys with '+'; composites 'hero:<id>', plugins 'hero:plugin:<name>:<id>', safety ops 'safety:<registry op name>'). An absent key resolves to nothing and stays inert (the dashboard.svelte.js rule); never rebound. Flip: require a role, i.e. drop the 'uid:' branch in controlKey and filter role-less fields out of placeableControls.
(3) Toggle stays bool-only even under the flag; RFC-080 item 5 (two-valued toggles on non-bool fields) and item 4 (per-placement narrowing) are NOT coded: they need placement config the layout store (ph-e82.3) does not carry yet.

title: Builder rulings owed: user-built home vs RENDERING §9/§11, cross-archetype presentation, law-10 keys, single fields vs nests
description:
Rulings the builder needs before the control contract (c) and the home page (d) are coded. DESIGN §10.1, §10.2. Each is a RENDERING conflict or an open product question; none is resolved in code.

1. User-built home vs derivation. RENDERING §11 "pages are derived from the catalog, never designed per app", §9 "a pattern's region assignment is part of its spec definition, never a per-app choice", and the §11 consistency invariant, against a user-arranged home where composites go wherever the user drops them. Proposed read: the home is an ADDITIONAL user surface; the derived category pages stay and keep every field reachable (§12), so the invariant holds for the derived tree. Needs an operator ruling and, if accepted, a Valence RFC stating a user-authored surface is conformant (never code against an unaccepted clause).
2. Presentation across archetypes. Knob, bar, segmented are projections inside one archetype (settings.js WIDGET already has such variants). slider vs stepper (§8.2 rows 9/10) and readout vs graph (rows 12/13 vs row 15) cross an archetype boundary that §8.2 decides by the first matching row. Ruling: allow as a user override (RFC), or restrict the offered set to the derived archetype's projections.
3. Law 10 keys. A single-field control with no role has only its uid (channel id + field name) as a stable key, which is wire vocabulary. Ruling: accept uid (inert when absent, the dashboard.svelte.js rule) or require a role for placement outside the derived pages.
4. Single fields placeable anywhere vs only inside nests (operator: undecided).

TEST/VALIDATION PLAN: none (decision). Each ruling is recorded as a dated comment here, then written into DESIGN §10 with an amendments row in the same commit; RFCs filed in Valence RFC-QUEUE where item 1 or 2 is accepted.
acceptance_criteria: Four rulings recorded as dated comments and written into DESIGN §10; any accepted RENDERING change filed as a Valence RFC.

title: Builder (a): top strip replaces OS decorations, ShellBar and the bottom safety dock; mandatory e-stop; full width
description:
Phase (a), DESIGN §10.3 and §10.4. One top strip replaces three things: the OS title bar (tauri.conf.json window gets decorations false; capabilities/default.json gains the window permissions for drag, minimize, maximize, close), ShellBar.svelte (discovery and transport merge into the strip), and SafetyBar.svelte's bottom dock (.safetydock is fixed bottom:0 under 960px and the last flex row above it; both move to the top). The strip carries the mandatory e-stop (SafetyBar fixedCtls, bound by identity, law 2) which edit mode cannot remove, the global refusal surface (lastRefusal) and the unattended chip. Every other safety op becomes a placeable module in phase (c); until then they stay in the strip. Full width: drop .app max-width 1680px (style.css); prose keeps its measure. T22: one strip, one top reserve, it alone absorbs safe-area-inset-top; the bottom reserve (--dock-h) goes. Served page: the same strip without window controls. Absorbs ph-gf8's width half; its zoom half moves to (b).

TEST/VALIDATION PLAN (device-free first):
- test/responsive-matrix.mjs: new asserts at every viewport and tab: exactly one stop-archetype e-stop inside the top strip, its rect fully on screen after scrolling every scroll container to its end (law 11), no fixed bar at the bottom edge, content width at 3840x2160 and 2560x1440 equals the window minus gutters.
- test/safety-reach.test.mjs: e-stop reachable from every view and renderer class; with a watch-tier session (role-exempt); still present while a confirm modal is open (§8.4 stop row).
- test/shell-chrome-geometry.test.mjs: one reserve, flush stacking, a single safe-area owner, both scroll modes (T22).
- Live against valencesim (test/actions-live.test.mjs pattern): press the strip e-stop, read the latch on a second raw session.
- Shell by hand on Windows, screenshots in test/evidence/: drag, double-click maximize, Snap Layouts on the maximize button, minimize, close, resize from every edge.
acceptance_criteria: Shell on Windows runs undecorated with working window controls; one strip carries discovery, transport, the non-removable e-stop, refusals and the unattended chip; no bottom dock; .app spans the window at 16:9; the listed suites pass.
notes: 2026-10-09 triage: NEEDS THE OPERATOR: the by-hand shell checks are the only thing holding this chain (close gate: X, Alt+F4, taskbar close, hold on touch; the top bar as drag region). A yes here lets ph-e82.2, .3, .4, .5 and .6 close (each note says 'close once' the previous closes); ph-e82.17, ph-e82.22 (veto pass) and ph-vdk.53 (live shell smoke) wait on the same session.

comments.text:
Live-verified against Nucleus 631f31d valencesim (42-entry catalog, pattern plane present), test/actions-live.test.mjs, commit 1e0f008. Both viewports (390x844 touch, 1280x800 mouse).

PASS [verified 2026-09-25 -- node test/actions-live.test.mjs against valencesim --homed --port 8882 --http 8880]:
- Actions card renders the pattern-presets-cmd action.preset trigger (save/load/delete/rename, only non-persistent action.* this catalog advertises; no has_drive machine-admin here)
- choosing a pattern tile writes pattern-state.pattern on the wire, matches UI
- roster count (0x1220) increments on save and decrements on delete, matching wire
- PatternWidget run/stop sets pattern-state.running and (this run) moved the carriage on 0x1100
- background_run: Cancel snaps back with no write; Confirm sends the write and the applied value echoes; confirm overlay body is the catalog's own desc text
- a second session sees the SafetyBar Unattended chip once the owning session leaves with background_run still on
- Confirm layer: no reboot/reset-tagged actions exist in this catalog (has_drive absent) -- noted, not skipped silently

LEFT OPEN, two related findings (both documented inline in the test with wire evidence, not silently weakened):
1. A pattern-presets-cmd SAVE sent from the browser gets a well-formed ECHO from the hub (captured via CDP framereceived, decoded FRAME.ECHO ch=0x3220 applied={1:1,2:slot,3:name} within ms) but the ActionField shadow never leaves 'pending' -- session.sendIntent's promise never resolves. The identical payload from a plain Node session (with or without a real /uitoken token, with light or heavy subscription load) gets its echo in ~10-15ms. Reproduces only inside a browser runtime. Suspect Valence/clients/js/session.js's echo/intent correlation, not ActionField or runAction (both are straight pass-throughs).
2. Loading the saved slot does not actually recall the saved value (checked via 0x1210 master, an ordinary captured field) even though load's own confirmed-text arrives normally. Roster count mechanics (create/destroy the slot) work correctly on both save and delete. Likely the same root cause as (1) rather than a second bug.

Neither looks like a Phosphor UI defect -- everything Phosphor itself renders and drives matches the wire. Recommend a follow-up bead against the Valence client library once triaged there.

comments.author: AtlanticTM
comments.text:
ROOT CAUSES (both findings closed, commit 831ca60).
1. Save never confirmed: NOT the Valence library. src/model/shadow.svelte.js ensureShadow did `sh = shadows[k] = {...}`; the assignment expression yields the RAW object, not the $state proxy, so every transition on the FIRST write to a shadow key bypassed Svelte signals (settle after the ECHO, and writeSetting/sendCommand overdue/fail timers). CDP capture showed INTENT seq=1 intent_id=1 and ECHO intent_id=1 correlating correctly; the promise resolved, the UI just never saw it. Load worked only because save had already created the record. Fix: assign, then read back through shadows[k].
2. Load did not recall master: test assumption. Nucleus flagship_p4/src/patterns/PatternSettings.h capturePreset() snapshots in/out speed, in/out accel and modifier lanes, never master; reproduced identically from plain Node. Marker switched to in_speed (0x3210 key 5).

title: Generic readouts never dim on staleness; telemetry chart fabricates a held line (laws 8, 9, T18)
description:

Field readouts ignore sampleTs and the link phase, so after a link drop every generic card keeps showing the last value at full contrast. TelemetryChart samples the retained snapshot every animation frame and stamps it with performance.now(), so a dead link draws a flat, confident line instead of a gap, and a clumped burst is re-timed to render time (T18). Its default roles are position and velocity only, so the power/current/temperature lanes its header promises are never drawn.

EVIDENCE: Field.svelte:29-47 (no freshness input), RailWidget.svelte:278-325 and HeroNumerals.svelte:212 (the only stale handling), TelemetryChart.svelte:124-133 (sample() pushes reportedValue at render time), :33 (default roles), App.svelte:232 (mounted with defaults), machine.svelte.js:399-405 (sampleTs exists). RENDERING.md §13 laws 8/9, §8.4 chart ("missing samples render as GAPS"), §10 scope, .claude/rules/webui.md T18.

ACCEPTANCE: one freshness rule (per channel, against its granted rate) applied to every value surface; stale values dim with a text reason, not color alone; the chart pushes on STATE arrival with reconstructed source time and draws a gap across silence; lanes come from telemetry.* roles the catalog carries. telebuf-sim-style regression for the chart.

A phone renders every card of a 40-field category stacked; a 4K window renders the same tree at the same density. title: A confirmed control shows the pre-write value until the STATE push lands: displayValue ignores the ECHO's applied value
description: Found restoring browser-check (ph-c3fj, lp/hygiene2, 2026-10-10). src/model/shadow.svelte.js documents 'the moment the ECHO lands we display the APPLIED value', and sendQueued stores sh.applied, but displayValue returns reportedValue(field, sample) for every non-pending status, so between the ECHO and the STATE push that carries the new value a control reads confirmed while showing the old value. Fix: show sh.applied while confirmed until the field's channel takes a STATE push after the ECHO; control-contract gets a fake-hub mode whose STATE lags the ECHO.

title: Funscript A-B loop: the seam span collapses when A or B lands beside a knot
description:
The seam is one span from the last knot before b to the first knot after a (FUNSCRIPT.md Loop, scheduler.js timeline()). Its length is (b - that knot) + (that knot - a), so a point pressed a few ms beside a knot leaves a seam of a few ms that still has to cross the script's jump between b and a.

Measured on valencesim (Nucleus 105e6fb, window 0..500 mm), live-playback staircase 20..80 by 15: A was pressed 21 ms before the knot at 37421 ms (pos 65), and B 42 to 85 ms after the knot at 41407 (pos 50). The seam lasted 63 to 95 ms for 0.15 of the window. The plan's speed reached 2.2 to 2.4 window/s, and the position moved 0.072 to 0.080 of the window per 35 ms sample, about 1100 mm/s, on every wrap. Plain play stepped 0.016. When A landed 13 ms after that knot, the next knot came 501 ms on, the seam was 574 ms and the step was 0.029.

This is the documented design: the rail follows one span and never teleports. Still, on a machine it is a jolt at the planner's limits each lap, and A-B points land within 50 ms of a knot often, since spans are about 400 ms. Options for a ruling:
(a) a minimum seam length: skip the first knot after a, or the last before b, when the seam would be shorter than about one span or the seek glide's seekMs;
(b) keep the design and note the cost (veto-able, as the Loop bullet is).

ph-rr35's test now presses A and B mid-span, so the seam is the staircase's own step.

(1) PlanStrip, RailWidget and the health frame counter run requestAnimationFrame every display frame while nothing moves: about 20 ms/s of the 85-100 ms/s idle main thread at 60 Hz, four times that at 240 Hz. (2) PlanStrip sizeIfNeeded reads clientWidth every frame; behind the player's DOM writes that forces a layout, about 28 ms/s while playing (a ResizeObserver would read it once per resize). (3) plugins.svelte.js trialPending() walks every catalog entry and layout through the $state proxies on each call (the player's status reads it every tick); with motion.js record() (catalog proxies per segment) it is the largest allocator left that survives into the old generation while playing. Fix: memoize the meta.trial_pending fields per catalog, read samples raw; same for record's layout reads.
close_reason: lp/shellperf 8921b15 + 9508b14 (unmerged). RailWidget and PlanStrip loops on demand (wake on a new value, freshness flip, map/theme/resize; rail settles 1 s after nothing changes, plan span view lingers for its 1.2 s ghost fade), PlanStrip size from a ResizeObserver, activity polled on arrival + deadline timer. Health fps: a 6-frame burst once a second (keeps the card, ring and evidence meaningful at idle; idle Health card reads 60 fps). trialPending by role index, gate entryOf per-catalog Map, motion door plain stream shape per catalog. stallprobe valencesim 60 Hz headless, 20 s, mean of 2 runs, main ms/s: About 80->59, Dash 104->77, player idle 73->56, playing 275->267 (noise; rAF ms/s 101->49), paused 84->61; idle rAF/s 240->66; minor GC playing 7.5->1, Dash 35->17; majors unchanged; tasks >12 ms 0-1 -> 0. Rail wake latency 13 ms (< one frame). Remaining per-frame costs: ph-oh2n (player frameSource), ph-p8yz (TelemetryChart); allocations: ph-54gs.
