title: Add to Dash: a submenu over the named layouts, New Dash, check and show
description: Operator ruling 2026-10-10 with the same-day correction: Phosphor's Dashes are the named layouts (dashboard.svelte.js layouts, orderedLayoutNames, switchLayout, addLayout); nothing parallel is built. Add to Dash in the field and module context menus opens a submenu listing orderedLayoutNames and ending with New Dash... (addLayout, the inline naming flow). A layout that holds the item shows a check; choosing it switches to it (switchLayout via the Dash tab) and scrolls to the card. An add writes through the store and grid.js placement at the first free spot; an unbuilt layout first copies its seed. Keyboard: ArrowRight or Enter opens the submenu, ArrowLeft or Escape closes it; touch: a tap opens it inline. Non-full classes: as today (ph-e82.7), the item only where the result can be seen. Seams: src/ui/contextmenu.js, src/plugins/kit.js menu, src/ui/Home.svelte, src/model/dashboard.svelte.js.
acceptance_criteria: Suites at 1428x900, 1024x768 and 420x860, dark and Paper: add to an unbuilt Default keeps its seed; add to a New Dash...; the check and scroll for a placed item; the keyboard and touch paths; reload persistence; DESIGN 10.1 and 10.13 amendment rows; npm run check at zero findings.
notes: Veto-able calls (agent, 2026-10-10): (1) the seed copy runs on every unbuilt layout, not only Default: a layout made by + Add layout shows the same seed, so an add there would make it vanish too. (2) New Dash… holds only the item: its seed was never on screen. (3) An add leaves the user on the page and says 'Added to <Dash>' in the status slot; only a checked Dash navigates (opens it with the card's first control focused). (4) Off the full class Add to Dash is absent (every layout draws its seed there, ph-e82.7) instead of the suggested read-only one-column Dashes; nothing on those classes changed. (5) The flyout opens on hover too, closing 300 ms after the pointer leaves for another item unless it reaches the flyout. (6) New Dash… names in place in the submenu (placeholder 'Dash name', 'Name taken'), not in the rail. (7) Held adds are keyed per layout so an add to a layout not on screen is written when its grid measures it. (8) registerMenu items stay one row: no plugin submenus.

title: Neutrino fleet soak: 1024 wasm Neutrino hubs in one node host (worker_threads) hammered by randomized headless Valence clients; health/anomaly counters collected; ramp to find the knee
description: Operator 2026-10-09: 1024 locally (cloud 16000 later). Design (Fable): one node process, N worker_threads each hosting ~32 Neutrino wasm instances (src/model/integral/* bytes + loader: each instance has private memory so the hub's process-wide singletons are isolated); one tick loop per worker drives integral_tick(now) for its hubs (1 ms nominal; measure lateness); clients are headless valence-js sessions over in-memory ports (the bridge contract from integral-bridge.js / sim/valencesim/wasm/check.mjs IntegralSocket+pump), one or two per hub, each with a seeded random personality: stream a funscript (free knots, rests at reversals), jog, drag the window mid-stream, toggle the oscillator, pause/resume, estop/release, disconnect/reconnect, inject latency/loss/reorder at the bridge. Collect per hub: kinetic-diag counters (plans, failures, anomalies by kind, plan_us), planner stalls/late plans, protocol errors/NACKs, session reaps, heap of each wasm instance; per client: send lead, refusals; aggregate per minute; flag any hub with a fault, a stuck session, a non-monotonic counter or a crash (trap). Ramp 32 -> 1024 and report the knee (tick lateness p99 vs hub count, CPU, RSS). Seeds reproducible: any failing hub is re-runnable alone by seed. Lives in Phosphor test/fleet/ (or a tools/fleet/ in Nucleus if better: decide and say why).
notes:
FLEET RESULTS 2026-10-10 (lane lp/fleet: 9c41e41 c602126 736fb53 dd2503e, unmerged). Neutrino = the vendored integral pin (Nucleus 4226af7, 0.1.34-p4hub). Host 9950X3D 16C/32T 62 GB, SHARED with other agents' browser suites (host CPU 30-55 % before the fleet started), so lateness is pessimistic.
Home: Phosphor test/fleet/, not Nucleus: it soaks the pair the app ships, Phosphor's own client stack (valence-js session, src/model/motion.js door, the funscript player's scheduler) against the vendored Neutrino pin; a Nucleus home would have to borrow Phosphor's client code.

RAMP (5 min a step, 1-2 seeded clients a hub; p99 = tick lateness, median minute of the worst worker; work = time in ticks, drains and client steps per worker):

KNEE: polling workers, not hubs. Past the 16 physical cores (a 1 ms poller on an SMT sibling, or preempted, waits out a 15.6 ms Windows quantum) p99 jumps: 24 workers 4.3 ms, 30 workers 23 ms (max 1.3 s). On 16 workers 1024 hubs hold p99 1.4 ms at 54 % work: this PC hosts 1024 Neutrinos with headroom (about 1,500 at 80 % work, projected). The default now caps workers at the physical cores. 17.1 MB of wasm memory per hub (reserved; RSS 2.6 GB at 1024).

LONG RUNS (0 traps, 0 session reaps, 0 stuck or stalled sessions, 0 intent timeouts, 0 ring drops in both):
- 512 hubs x 30 min, 16 workers: healthy every minute, p99 0.17-7.2 ms (worst minute with the host at 98 %), RSS flat 1.7-2.0 GB; 1.05 M actions, 693 k segments, 4.1 M plans; NACKs all honest (SOURCE_CONFLICT 94k, INTERLOCK 48k, TRIAL_CONFLICT 33k, UNSUPPORTED_OP 24k, NOT_HOMED 16k, INVALID_VALUE 13k, ESTOP_ACTIVE 3.5k, TAKEOVER_REQUIRED 615, CLEAR_REFUSED 29).

BUGS FILED: Nucleus val-8yv P2 (a max_rail write does not hold the window inside it, SPEC 9.6; 0x1000 publishes a window past max_rail; on ~3/4 of hubs; repro `--replay 3`), val-hnq P2 (a classic pattern in a narrow window re-plans every hub tick, 200 plans/s, an anomaly on every second plan, carriage parked; `--replay 388 --minutes 10`, ~441 s), val-ku3 P2 (0x4100 motion-anomaly declared, never emitted), val-vik P3 (plan-strip norms u16 x 10000: a plan outside the window saturates at 6.5535); Valence rfc-zvh9 P2 (the library's 8-field INTENT cap is unadvertised: pattern-advanced-cmd 59 keys, osc-set 16 keys at Nucleus 0.1.38, get MALFORMED).

title: Catalog page layout pass: how the generated pages (Motion, System, Setup...) lay out their cards and fields
description: Operator 2026-10-09 with a desktop screenshot of the Motion page on Virtual (C:/Users/Atlan/AppData/Local/Temp/claude/c--Users-Atlan-Documents-OpenValence/44929813-8ccf-4a6d-8409-d0b241e8f350/images/67.png): 'perhaps we have a look at how these pages and etc get laid out'. ui-pass formula: feedback first, then design, lanes, verify.
notes:
FABLE OBSERVATIONS on the screenshot (veto-able, for the pile): (1) the Diagnostics card spans the full width for ONE field (asked position) and leaves a huge empty band under it beside the tall Oscillator card: the grid packs by rows, not by height; (2) the Tuning section's cards have unequal heights and leave holes (Motion behavior / Stream ingress, Curve, Ceilings / Plan time, Active plan, Planner); (3) labels are raw field names (anom endvel clamped, sync seg bundles, plan us last, chase dense ms) instead of plain words; (4) internal wire bookkeeping shown to users: 'settings on trial' (trial_mask) twice, 'flags' as a dot list, 'reset counter'; (5) units and formats: '0.00 us', '0 norm', 'norm/s'; (6) the Ceilings card's trim max stepper is oversized vs the other rows; the Curve card's 'crisp at 0' label reads as a sentence fragment for smoothness; (7) the Oscillator card stacks with large vertical gaps (label row, then control row, then value chip on its own row). Questions for the operator: which of these are wrong to you, and what should a generated page look like.
OPERATOR RULING 2026-10-09 (relayed by the coordinator, verbatim): "it has to be valence conforming; how categories are laid out in terms of aligning to a screen is a client choice; keep both in mind". Reading for the proposal: every item splits into (A) what Valence decides and Phosphor honors exactly (membership, order, labels, units, ranks, roles, what must or must not show; cited) and (B) Phosphor's own choice (packing, columns, widths, density, screen alignment, responsive), never contradicting (A). A fix that needs the catalog to carry more is an RFC or a Nucleus catalog fill, never a client guess; anything hidden from users is justified by a spec clause or the device-knowledge rule, not taste.
SURVEY 2026-10-09: ROOT CAUSES (read-only). Screenshots of Generator, Motion, System, Setup at 2767x1813, 1976x1295@1.4 (matches the operator's card pitch), 1428x900, 1024x768, 420x860, dark, native valencesim, in test/evidence/responsive-catalog-layout/: first-run state as <page>-<size>.png, the operator's state (terse, adv on, diag on) as op-<page>-<size>.png. test/evidence/catalog-layout/ is NOT gitignored; responsive*/ is, hence that path.

HOW A CATALOG PAGE LAYS OUT TODAY. settings.js pass 3 (settings.js:561-623) buckets fields by category, then by group string, diagnostic fields into groups of their own; order = catalog order, unsectioned cards first, each section's cards together, diagnostic groups last within each run. App.svelte:498-514 turns groups into items: a section header item before each section's first card; the ungrouped card is titled "Settings", the ungrouped diagnostic card "Diagnostics" (App.svelte:507). DashGrid places them with the rank seed, place(all, {}, cols, null, fitH) (DashGrid.svelte:151) into grid.js pack (grid.js:114): each card is seeded at its floor width s0 = max(measured min-content, 8 layout columns = 16 rem) (DashGrid.svelte:315, rclass.js:44) and its measured height at that width; it takes the first free rect scanning rows from the previous card's row down (the monotonic "from", grid.js:116, 131), left to right; then the card ending each row stretches to the right edge (grid.js:140-147); then cards fall straight up (grid.js:148-151). A section header is a full-width one-cell row (DashGrid.svelte:254 seeds it at 0, so the default width is cols). Inside a card, .card-body is a flex wrap with each field's basis = the field floor (style.css:797-798): one field column at the floor width, N columns when stretched. A field row (Field.svelte:604ff): head = label group (label, adv/restart tags, i, reset) + status slot + value chip, then the control.

(1) Diagnostics full width, empty band. Diagnostics (raw_10um, the only diagnostic field of ungrouped 0x1100) is the 3rd card of the unsectioned run, so it ends row 1 and the row-end stretch (grid.js:140-147) hands it every leftover column for one field. The Tuning header is a full-width row, so it lands under the run's lowest card (Oscillator) and nothing can sit beside Oscillator. Fix (Phosphor, B): no stretch-to-edge on seeded pages; leftover row width widens the tallest card instead (proposal note). Not a catalog problem.

(2) Holes in Tuning. Same pack: first fit with the monotonic "from" (no card above the previous card's row), unequal heights, and one stretched wide-short card per row (Re-planning, Planner); fall-up only moves straight up. Fix (B): height-aware masonry per section run (proposal note).

(3) Raw names. labelFor (format.js:80) = role label (roles.js:165), else descLabel (format.js:102: the desc's first clause when 2-3 words and at most 30 chars), else humanize(name) (settings.js:214: underscore to space, ovr/cfg/ff expanded); style.css:853 lowercases. anom_endvel_clamped, sync_seg_bundles, plan_us_last, chase_dense_ms have prose descs, so they fall to the humanized wire name. SPEC 8.8 has NO label annotation; SPEC 1.2 item 7 says the label comes from the hub, which today means the field name (24 B max) plus desc (128 B max). The words are Nucleus's (A): rename the fields to words with no unit baked in (the unit is its own annotation), a catalog fill with no RFC; or an RFC adds an optional label annotation if the operator wants terse keys. Rename cost: Dash placements keyed uid:<channel>:<name> of a renamed field go inert (law 10, DESIGN 10.2); Nucleus tests that name them. Client side: only retiring descLabel (6b).

(4) Bookkeeping. trial_mask (meta.trial_pending) shows twice per page (0x1030 + 0x1122 on Motion, 0x1000 + 0x1120 on Setup) because settings.js:455 drops only meta.enabled_mask ("machinery, never drawn") and nothing consumes trial_pending per field (only history.svelte.js:53 and plugins.svelte.js:140 read it); its bits are labeled with wire names. "flags" is 0x1100's own field (no role, rank detail, "Live machine mode bits"): real machine state, not bookkeeping; the client may not hide it. "reset counter" is meta.reset_gen (ROLE_LABEL, roles.js:189) on 0x1111 kinetic-diag, an entry ranked diagnostic, like every anom_/sync_/plan-time/planner counter and the Active plan card (0x1110): collapsed by default, seen only because diag was on, conformant. Spec: RENDERING 8.5 and 11, "every field MUST stay reachable through the derived pages"; RENDERING 4, hidden = never rendered (inert fields only), diagnostic = collapsed by default; SPEC 8.8 trial marks, "a client MAY mark those values". So hiding a mask by taste is out, and Phosphor's existing enabled_mask drop (settings.js:455) is itself an unratified reading. Fix: (A) Nucleus ranks enabled_mask and trial_mask diagnostic (AUTHORING 4); an RFC clarifies that a meta.enabled_mask / meta.trial_pending field is rendered through the fields it indexes (gray, trial mark), which also covers the existing drop. (B) Phosphor marks each on-trial field from the bits. The ungrouped card's title "Settings" over a card that holds no setting is Phosphor's (App.svelte:507).

(5) Units. "0.00 us" is plan_us_avg (f32, unit_id 24, no step) taking precisionFor's 2-decimal default (format.js:112-121); (B) fix: whole microseconds, the unit's resolution (RENDERING 6 SHOULD), UNIT_ID.us added at format.js:113; autorange to ms is a MAY (RFC-086). "norm", "norm/s", "flag", "1/s3", "1/s", "1/s2", "m" are free strings with no unit_id, and RENDERING 6 makes the client render them verbatim (MUST). (A) Nucleus fill: unit_id 4 (0-1) on start/end/cur_norm (scaled to 0..1) and on oscillator amplitude; 14 (count) on every counter (plans, failures, anom_*, sync_*; the roster's count/capacity/generation carry the string "count" with no id); distance in mm by scale (no m in the registry); no "flag" string on bitfields. norm/s and the normalized ceilings 1/s^n have no registry unit: the firmware converts to the mm/s family, or an RFC adds them before the tag (RENDERING 14).

(6a) trim max. 0.1..1 by 0.05 = 18 ticks, under DRAG_TICKS_MIN 20 (settings.js:80), so RENDERING 8.2 row 10 stepper: the archetype is right. The size: a full-width .og-num with sp-3 padding (style.css:676) between 34 px nudges (style.css:902-922), a row of its own, beside sliders that carry a small head chip. (B) fix: a field's stepper takes the head chip's metrics and slot, minus and plus beside it, one row; 40 px targets kept under a coarse pointer (law 12).

(6b) "crisp at 0" is descLabel taking "Crisp at 0" from "Crisp at 0, smooth at 1" (format.js:102-110); likewise cycles a second, rendering now, peak displacement, asked position, jerk ceiling override. A shape heuristic over prose is a client guess: (B) retire descLabel; label = role label, else the name. Ship it with the Nucleus renames, since raw_10um and the *_ovr fields read worse without them.

(7) Oscillator gaps. Every seeded card sits at the 16 rem field floor (rclass.js:44), under the 18 rem compact boundary (Field.svelte:1314), so every field on a category page draws the compact head, a fixed two-row grid (Field.svelte:1315-1320, rows 18px and minmax(20px, auto)): label, then status words + value chip, then the control. A toggle, segmented or indicator has no chip, so row 2 is a blank 20 px band (above "off", under "shape", under "settings on trial"); a readout puts its value alone on row 2. At 1024x768 the Oscillator is the stretched row-end card, crosses 18 rem and draws one-row heads (op-motion-1024x768.png). (B) fix: read-only fields one row (label left, value right); a toggle's switch takes the chip slot; the seed floor and the compact boundary reconciled.

(8, extra) The segmented "saw_reverse" button overflows the Oscillator card at the floor width (the operator's shot, and 1428, 1976@1.4, 2767 here): the min-content measure misses the segmented row. Not traced.
SURVEY 2026-10-09: LAYOUT MODEL PROPOSAL, split per the operator's ruling into (A) Valence decides, Phosphor honors exactly, and (B) Phosphor's own choice, never contradicting (A). Veto-able.

1. Membership and order. (A) One category = one page (RENDERING 3, 11); a card per group string, ungrouped fields in a default card (SPEC 8.9 item 2); a section is the text before the first " / " (RENDERING 3, RFC-096); order is authoring order: channels ascending, fields in layout order (SPEC 8.9 item 4, RENDERING 11); diagnostic last or collapsed (RENDERING 9); rank hidden never drawn, advanced behind an affordance and never removed (RENDERING 4); an echo pair and a tagged min/max pair are one control (RENDERING 11). (B) The default card's title; where sections sit among unsectioned cards (RENDERING 3 calls that the renderer's craft); card numbers show the catalog order.

2. Packing. (B) Height-aware masonry inside each section run: cards in catalog order, each to the column span whose bottom is highest, ties to the left; a section header stays a full-width barrier under its run; DOM and tab order stay catalog order. A fixed row grid wastes height whenever card heights differ, which a catalog page always has. (A) check: RENDERING 9 makes geometry the renderer's craft and RENDERING 11 says "within a section: catalog declaration order"; placement order = catalog order, numbered, is the reading. Operator rules on it.

3. Card width from content. (B) Widths in whole field floors: every card starts at one floor; the row's leftover width goes to its tallest card, one floor at a time while it has more fields than floors, until heights level or the width runs out; no row-end stretch to the edge. A wide control (segmented, range, composite) raises its own floor by measurement. Applies to seeded category pages only; the Dash keeps its saved rects (law 10). Replaces grid.js:140-147's stretch there.

4. What never renders. (A) only: rank hidden (RENDERING 4); diagnostic collapsed until asked (RENDERING 4, 9); everything else reachable (RENDERING 8.5, 11). For the masks: Nucleus ranks enabled_mask and trial_mask diagnostic now (AUTHORING 4, no RFC); an RFC clarifies that a meta.* index field is rendered through the fields it indexes before Phosphor drops one as a value; meanwhile Phosphor marks trial fields (SPEC 8.8 MAY). Counters are already authored diagnostic: conformant. No client taste list.

5. Labels. (A) The registered role's label (Phosphor's table keyed by role, SPEC 8.8 "roles as opportunities"), else the field name under one fixed rule (underscore to space); no prose heuristics, so descLabel goes. The words are Nucleus's: fields renamed to words with units out of the names, or an RFC label annotation if terse keys must stay. (B) Casing (lowercase by CSS), one-line ellipsis, the aspect/scope tag (RENDERING 5).

6. Units. (A) unit_id wins; a free string renders verbatim (RENDERING 6 MUST); Nucleus fills unit_id everywhere (count, 0-1, µs) and converts or RFCs the normalized rates. (B) Precision by the unit's resolution (whole count, bytes, µs; physical quantities 0-2 decimals by step), optional autorange (RFC-086 MAY), 0-1 as percent where a role calls for it.

7. Field row density. (A) Law 5's ladder with its text reason and no layout shift, law 8 stale dimming, law 12's 40 px targets on a coarse pointer. (B) The two rungs stay (DESIGN 10.12), but read-only fields take one row (label left, value right); a writable field keeps its status slot without a blank band (a toggle in the chip slot, a stepper at chip size); and the seed floor (16 rem) and the compact boundary (18 rem) are reconciled: either the floor rises to 18 rem so seeded cards draw normal, or compact is redrawn as above.

QUESTIONS FOR THE OPERATOR: Q1 masonry with numbered placement order as the reading of RENDERING 11's "catalog declaration order": yes? Q2 leftover width to the tallest card, or uniform card widths? Q3 human labels: Nucleus renames fields (no RFC, Dash placements of renamed fields go inert), or an RFC label annotation? Q4 masks: Nucleus ranks enabled_mask/trial_mask diagnostic plus an RFC clarification; and Phosphor's existing enabled_mask drop, keep it until the RFC or restore it? Q5 the motion "flags" bits (homed, homing, gen_running, paused, override, estop, stream): Nucleus keeps them detail, groups them, or ranks them diagnostic? Q6 norm/s and the 1/s^n ceilings: firmware converts to mm/s units, or an RFC adds units before the tag? Q7 density: seeded cards at the normal rung (floor 18 rem), or the compact rung redrawn? Q8 the ungrouped card's title ("Settings" today, even when it holds no setting)?
2026-10-10, Valence RFC-112 (draft): if ruled in, the oscillator amplitude fields carry unit_id 0 (mm) with max 1000, no longer unit_id 4 / 0-1; lane lp/oscmm.

title: Health: the 2 Hz CLOCK shares the session's one CLOCK slot with motion.js's sync burst
description: Valence clients/js session.js keeps one pendingClock and its reply handler does not match t0, so a second syncClock() while one is in flight takes the first's reply and the first times out null; motion.js's hunt (CLOCK_HUNT exchanges at 'live' and the door's first use) stops early on a null. health.svelte.js skips its 2 Hz exchange while another exchange is recent (600 ms), which narrows but cannot close the race (the first hunt exchange after 'live' has no prior). Fix belongs in clients/js syncClock (queue or reject a concurrent call, match the echoed t0); that is a Valence change through its own board, after which the guard in health.svelte.js can go.

title: Health reports: per-incident review, hold to send opens a prefilled public GitHub issue (diag-report), Save report file fallback, Sent reports log in About with removal
description:
Phosphor feature, no Valence RFC (fields come from Phosphor's own health ring, or read null until ph-9t5l's Health roles RFC lands). Operator final ruling 2026-10-09: a report is a conversation, so it becomes a public GitHub issue the user submits under their own account; Phosphor itself sends nothing. The GitHub account is the barrier to entry for now; an anonymous relay (Cloudflare Worker with a bot token) stays a much-later option, not designed here.

FLOW
1. An incident (ph-9t5l note, section 4) carries a snapshot (section 6). Its row on the Health page and the Log entry's expanded detail offer Send report.
2. Review screen (src/ui/ReportReview.svelte): the exact JSON the issue will carry, section by section, one row per field: plain name, what it is, why it helps, the value formatted, the raw JSON underneath. One table in src/model/report.js feeds both the rows and the builder, so no field can leave without a row. Below: Not included (script and video names, positions, times of day, hub name, addresses, session ids, tokens, log text), the privacy text, the size, Hold to send, Save report.
3. Hold to send: hold.js at 1500 ms; the button fills while held; release early opens nothing. On fire Phosphor opens, in the system browser (shell opener; served page window.open):
   https://github.com/openvalence/Phosphor/issues/new?template=diag-report.yml&title=Diagnostic%20report%20<id>&bundle=<encodeURIComponent(compact JSON)>
   Issue forms prefill a field by its id (GitHub form schema docs, checked 2026-10-09); the template applies the diag-report label. The user adds what happened in the form and presses Submit on GitHub: that is the final act.
4. URL budget: the encoded query stays under 7,500 characters (GitHub refuses much longer new-issue URLs). Over it, Phosphor saves the full bundle as diag-report-<id>.json (GitHub attachments take .json up to 25 MB), the URL carries the summary only (app, machine, incident, settings, evidence; no window series) with "attachment": "diag-report-<id>.json", the template asks to drag the file in, and the review screen says so before the hold. Window default: -60 to +30 s at 2 s steps plus 10 Hz stream signals over -2 to +0.5 s, which normally fits.
5. Save report: always offered; the same JSON to a file (shell save dialog; served page download link). The path for anyone without a GitHub account: share the file any way they like.
6. About > Sent reports (shell; the served page shows the same list at the foot of the Health page): id, date sent (local only, never in the bundle), size, View, Request removal. Stored in localStorage phosphor.reports.v1 as {id, issueUrl or null, sentAt, bytes, bundle}, try/catch on every access. The issue link resolves through the unauthenticated search API (GET api.github.com/search/issues?q=repo:openvalence/Phosphor+label:diag-report+in:title+<id>; 10 requests per minute per address; run when the row is shown and still unresolved), else a Paste link field.
7. Request removal: GitHub has no documented URL parameter that prefills a comment on an existing issue, so Phosphor copies /remove to the clipboard and opens the issue; the row reads "Paste /remove as a comment". The workflow deletes the issue; the row then reads Removed (the issues API answers 410 for a deleted issue). Forget drops the local row.

BUNDLE (phosphor.health-report/1; numbers and fixed enums only)

 "app":{"version":"0.1.0+233","platform":"windows|macos|linux|android|web","engine":"chromium-141","shell":true},
 "machine":{"firmware":"0.1.33-p4hub-bench","protocol":1,"transport":"ws|ble"},
 "incident":{"condition":"cutout|slow-link|busy|growth|...","cause":"client|network|hub|unknown|null","confidence":"decisive|likely","severity":"info|warn|act","count":3,"duration_ms":420},
 "settings":{"stream_buffer_ms":250,"schedule_latency_us":1000,"lookahead_ms":125},

 "window":{"from_ms":-60000,"to_ms":30000,"step_ms":2000,"series":{"rtt_ms":[],"lead_send_ms":[],"arrival_lead_ms":[],"downlink_gap_ms":[],"loop_lag_ms":[],"fps":[],"heap_mb":[],"rssi_dbm":[],"late_plans":[]},
   "fine":{"from_ms":-2000,"to_ms":500,"step_ms":100,"series":{"lead_send_ms":[],"owd_up_ms":[],"downlink_gap_ms":[]}}},
 "events":[{"t_ms":-1200,"kind":"cutout","cause":"network"}],

Time is milliseconds relative to the incident; no clock time, no date. id: 8 random base32 characters (crypto.getRandomValues). Free strings (versions, engine) match ^[0-9A-Za-z.+_-]{1,32}$. Positions, targets, script or media names, hub name, IP, session or instance ids, tokens, catalog content and log text are absent by construction: an allowlist builder, never a filter. What the user types on GitHub is theirs and outside the bundle.

PRIVACY TEXT
Short line (COPY.md): Public issue under your GitHub account
Detail: Send report opens a new public issue on github.com/openvalence/Phosphor in your browser, filled in with the report shown above. Nothing is sent until you press Submit there. It is posted under your own GitHub account, so anyone can read it and see who posted it, and GitHub shows when. The report holds no script or video names, no positions and no times of day: its times count from the moment of the problem. To take it down, comment /remove on the issue and it is deleted; only you, its author, can do that. No GitHub account? Save report keeps it as a file you can share any way you like.

FILES
- src/model/report.js: field table, builder, URL budget, save file, Sent reports store, issue lookup
- src/ui/ReportReview.svelte: review screen and Hold to send
- src/shell/AboutPane.svelte: Sent reports section (HealthPane renders the same list on the served page)
- test/report.test.mjs: builder, allowlist, URL budget and attachment fallback, the field-table coverage check
- .github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/diag-report.yml: name "Diagnostic report", labels [diag-report]; a markdown intro; textarea id bundle (label Report, render: json, required); textarea id happened (label What were you doing?, optional); markdown "If Phosphor saved a file, attach it here"
- .github/workflows/diag-report-remove.yml: on issue_comment created; if: the issue carries diag-report AND github.event.comment.user.login == github.event.issue.user.login AND the trimmed body is /remove (all inside the if: expression; comment text is never interpolated into run:); one step: gh api graphql deleteIssue(issueId: github.event.issue.node_id) with GH_TOKEN from secrets.DIAG_REMOVE_TOKEN; permissions: {} for GITHUB_TOKEN
- docs/DESIGN.md: one subsection under the Health section with these rulings

OPERATOR-OWNED SETUP
- secrets.DIAG_REMOVE_TOKEN: GITHUB_TOKEN cannot delete issues. deleteIssue needs a token whose user is an admin of openvalence/Phosphor, and the org setting that lets repository admins delete issues must be on. For a fine-grained PAT, scope it to Phosphor with Issues read/write; whether GitHub also wants Administration write for deleteIssue is to verify at setup.
- The audit trail is the workflow's run log (Actions keeps logs 90 days by default) plus the gap in issue numbers. If a permanent record is wanted, the workflow can also comment the removed number on a pinned "Removed reports" issue.
acceptance_criteria:
1) From an incident, Send report opens the review screen; every bundle field has a row (plain name, what, why, value, raw JSON), and a test fails if the builder emits a field the table lacks.
2) The bundle holds no script or media name, position, target, clock time or date, hub name, address, session or instance id, token or log text: a test seeds all of those into the ring and finds none in the output.
3) Hold to send fires only after 1500 ms held (pointer, touch, Enter/Space); a shorter hold opens nothing.
4) The opened URL is github.com/openvalence/Phosphor/issues/new?template=diag-report.yml with the title "Diagnostic report <id>" and the compact bundle in the bundle field; over the URL budget the full bundle is saved as diag-report-<id>.json, the URL carries the summary with attachment set, and the review says so before the hold.
5) Save report writes the same JSON with no account and no network.
6) About > Sent reports lists id, date (local only), size, View and Request removal; the issue link resolves by the title search or a pasted link; removal opens the issue with /remove on the clipboard.
7) .github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/diag-report.yml and .github/workflows/diag-report-remove.yml exist; the workflow deletes a diag-report issue only when its author comments /remove, never interpolates comment text into a shell, and reads its token from secrets.DIAG_REMOVE_TOKEN.
8) Short lines and the privacy text pass npm run check (copy-lint) with zero findings.

description: Operator 2026-10-08: the funscript player does not really carry the style of the rest of Phosphor. notes:
[style survey 1/10] ON-STATES WEAR --highlight, THE SHELL'S WEAR REALITY. Motion, Invert, the settings On/Off and Auto toggles and the analyzer's Preview take color+border --highlight when pressed-on (ui.js:664 .fsp-btn[aria-pressed=true]; interp.js:314; ui.js:1317). Shell: an on control is .og-btn.on / .og-seg button.active = --reality + --glow-reality (style.css .og-btn.on, .og-seg button.active); THEMES.md Accents: "Highlight never means a state: an active (on) control ... stay reality". Measured: .fsp-motion rgb(255,92,179) vs Motion page .og-seg active rgb(77,166,255). Under Paper (highlight follows reality) the same Motion button turns blue, so its meaning shifts with the theme. Shots: test/evidence/player-style/zoom2x-player-wave-bundle-dark.png vs zoom2x-ref-seg-active-dark.png; page-settings-dark-1428x900.png vs page-settings-light-1428x900.png; page-analyzer-dark-1428x900.png (Preview). The open tab (Player|Library, advpen's Advanced|Classic) in --highlight matches the documented advpen precedent and is NOT in this finding. PROPOSED RULING: a persistent on-state takes the shell's .on look (reality + glow); --highlight stays for focus, the momentary press and the open tab.
[style survey 2/10] THE PLUGIN SHIPS ITS OWN BUTTON CSS INSTEAD OF .og-btn. .fsp-btn (ui.js:659-665) plus two more private copies for the settings rows (interp.js:312-314, ui.js:1315-1317) restate .og-btn and drift: weight 400 vs 500, disabled opacity .4 vs .45, focus offset 1px vs the global 2px, hover/press missing the .og-btn:active highlight; the settings copies set font:inherit, so they render 17.92px against .og-btn's 14.69px (.82rem). The library already uses .og-btn (library.js:149, Save/Test), so one card shows two button families side by side. Measured: .fsp-motion 14.69px/400, .fsp-pset button 17.92px/400, .fsp-connect .og-btn 14.69px/500. Shots: page-loaded-dark-1428x900.png (library Save/Test vs Motion/Invert), zoom2x-player-settings-playback-dark.png, zoom2x-player-wave-bundle-dark.png vs zoom2x-ref-advpen-button-row-dark.png. PROPOSED RULING: every player button is .og-btn (.og-btn sm in the 28 px rows, its min-height reconciled with --fsp-bar), the three private button blocks are deleted; icon buttons keep only their glyph sizing.
[style survey 3/10] RAW FORM CONTROLS: THE OFFSET FIELD IS THE BROWSER'S DEFAULT NUMBER INPUT. ui.js:1014 builds input type=number with no class; .fsp-off input (ui.js:736) sets only size and font, so it renders the UA box: background rgb(59,59,59), 2 px rgb(133,133,133) border, radius 0, 17.92px mono (measured), a gray slab no other Phosphor surface has (white slab under Paper). Shell: .og-num, the recessed --screen numeral field (style.css .og-num), which Field.svelte's typeable chip and the advpen numeric twins use. The interp select likewise restyles to --bg-card at 17.92px (interp.js:307-308) where the shell select is --bg at .82rem. Shots: zoom2x-player-wave-bundle-dark.png and -light.png, zoom2x-player-settings-interp-dark.png vs zoom2x-ref-advpen-button-row-dark.png (native select). PROPOSED RULING: the offset input takes class og-num, the interp select drops its private background/font so the global select rule applies.
[style survey 4/10] THREE PRIVATE SLIDER THUMBS. interp.js:320-325, ui.js:1319-1324 (playback rows) and analyzer.js:144-150 each restate a rounded 9x20 pill thumb, radius 4.5px, 2 px --intent border, on --bg-card. The shell's range is one global rule: square 11x18 thumb (--slider-thumb-w/h), radius 0, --tx-val border, --highlight only while dragged or focused (style.css input[type=range]). The player's own volume sliders already get the shell thumb, so the card shows both shapes. Intent as the resting color also reads as "pending" in the ground-truth ladder. accent-color: var(--highlight) on .fsp-vol / .fsp-hb-vol (ui.js:721, 795) is dead, since the global rule sets appearance none. Out of scope: the timeline's scrub and range pills (timeline.js:180, 195) are advpen's documented handle vocabulary. Shots: zoom2x-player-settings-interp-dark.png vs zoom2x-ref-settings-chassis-dark.png; page-analyzer-dark-1428x900.png (Home speed row); zoom2x-player-transport-dark.png (volume thumb, shell shape). PROPOSED RULING: delete the three thumb blocks and the dead accent-color; settings and analyzer ranges take the global slider.
[style survey 5/10] HEADS AND LABELS USE THEIR OWN TYPE VOICE. Settings section heads (Motion curve, Playback) are h4 .85rem/600, sentence case, --tx-mut (interp.js:305, ui.js:1311): measured 15.23px/600/none. Shell heads are uppercase with tracking: card and pane head .8rem/500/uppercase/.12em/--tx-val (pane.css:39, DashItem .dash-title: 14.34px/500/uppercase/1.72px), sub-group title .card-sub .8rem/600/uppercase/.08em (style.css). Row labels .8rem/400 (interp.js:306, ui.js:1312; 14.34px) vs Field's .field-label .76rem/500/lowercase/.04em (13.62px); the shell itself mixes case here (ThemePicker's Hue/Brightness are sentence case), so the case is an operator call. PROPOSED RULING: section heads become .card-sub, analyzer group headers become .card-sub text without the band, row labels take the .field-label voice (operator picks the case).
[style survey 6/10] MONOSPACE ON WORDS. Readouts are fine: elapsed/remaining, rate, speed, offset digits and settings values in Martian Mono match the shell's .mono/output/.num rule, so there is no divergence there. The divergence is mono on words: the Open files button (library.js:61, .72rem mono, 12.9px, inside an .og-btn whose own face is Chakra 500), the zoom/A-B glyph buttons (timeline.js:203, mono 600), the analyzer's Lag/Plan/Kinetic status lines (analyzer.js:128, prose in mono), and the Search / Stash URL / API key inputs (library.js:55-56). The Funscript page draws the player bare on --bg. Its top row is the media name ("clip", .85rem --tx-mut, ui.js:677) where a native head would sit, and the library column and the settings section have no head or surface. The settings overlay is a third look: --bg-card plus a -4px drop shadow (page.js:40-43). Inside the Dash card, which already has the shell head "04 · FUNSCRIPT PLAYER", the player adds its own boxes: the status slot is a --bg-sunken box with a 1 px ring (ui.js:709-710), and the meter and stage are boxes too (ui.js:684, 703). PROPOSED RULING: the page gets shell heads (Player, Library, Settings) on surface-card, the settings section drops its shadow for the card surface, the status slot loses its own frame and keeps the 3 px tone bar.
[style survey 8/10] ROUND GEOMETRY ON A SQUARE INSTRUMENT. The shell's radius is 2 px, "the instrument look is square ... part of the identity" (style.css --radius comment), and thumbs and switch knobs are square. The player rounds: split bar radius 2px on a 4 px bar, so a pill (ui.js:691); glance ticks 1.5px (ui.js:705); analyzer row state markers 1.5px (analyzer.js:134); speed bar 1.5px (ui.js .fsp-speed i); the settings thumbs from note 4 at 4.5px. PROPOSED RULING: every player radius reads var(--r-s), 0 on bars and markers; the hover bar stays as ruled.
[style survey 9/10] TOKEN-RULE BREAKS IN THE LIBRARY. (a) .fsp-note[data-tone=warn], .fsp-status[data-tone=warn] { color: var(--warn) } (library.js:77) puts text in --warn. Law 13 and the player's own Look rule ("Text stays --tx: --warn is locked ... reads 1.8:1 on Paper's white card", FUNSCRIPT.md, The card) forbid it, and the shell's answer is --warn-ink (style.css). The suite's "no text in --warn" assert never reaches the library's Stash notes. (b) gap: ${GAP}px with GAP = 8 (library.js:45, 50, 53, 65, 81) is raw px spacing, banned by ph-acnj, and test/spacing-lint.mjs misses it because the template literal puts "${GAP}" before "px" and the lint's number regex never matches. Not shot: no Stash server here, so the warn tone did not render. PROPOSED RULING: --warn-ink (or --tx with the 3 px bar, as the status slot does) and var(--sp-3) for GAP; the lint learns to flag ${...}px.
[style survey 10/10] SETTINGS ROWS: LAYOUT SLIPS THE NATIVE ROW NEVER SHOWS. In the interp rows (interp.js grid 10ch | 1fr | 9ch), the Scale row's Auto button sits in the slider column and squeezes the slider to a stub, with the value pushed right (0.00-1.00). One row is labeled "No setting" with a bare slider and no value. The Curve select spans two columns at 17.92px. title: Funscript Auto Scale fits top and bottom separately from the twin's whole-script render; Auto default; overshoot hint on the curve modes
description:
Operator ruling 2026-10-08. The funscript player's Auto Scale fits the whole script symmetrically about the window center (interp.js fitGain on max|p - 0.5|, FUNSCRIPT.md "Scale", ph-6e36). Scripts overshoot the top only, the bottom only, or both; a symmetric gain shrinks both ends for an overshoot at one.

Wanted:
1. Auto fits top and bottom separately from the twin's whole-script render: the analyzer's wall-free measure (analyzer.js wideExtent) reports the planner's min and max share over the whole script, not one excursion; the correction is the affine map that pulls only the ends that leave the window: lower = min(0, pmin), upper = max(1, pmax), p' = (p - lower) / (upper - lower), on the 0.01 grid as today. A script that only overshoots the top keeps its bottom actions where they are. The curve estimate before the twin lands (curveExtent) reports min and max the same way.
2. Auto is the default (INTERP.scaleAuto true). Saved prefs that carry scaleAuto false stay as saved (no stomping).
3. The overshooting modes (Catmull-Rom, Hermite, Akima, Makima, and the hub's smooth/G2 style once it is on the wire, kin-tnv) get one terse hint in the interp card: they reach past the actions, so the fit shrinks the range to keep the curve inside the window. One fragment, Blender tooltip rule (docs/DESIGN.md), no story.
4. The readout under Auto shows the fit in force: top and bottom, e.g. "auto 0.03..0.96" (or the two gains), never a story.
5. The manual Scale slider stays one symmetric gain (operator did not ask for two sliders). Say so in FUNSCRIPT.md.
6. The wire, the drawn curve and the Kinetic preview all run on the mapped actions, as today; the scheduler's handoff slopes scale with the map.

Whole-script visibility is required for the fit, so this stays client-side in Phosphor (the hub never sees the whole script, SPEC 10 keeps kinematics on the hub but the fit is authoring, not kinematics).

Acceptance: FUNSCRIPT.md Scale section rewritten to the asymmetric fit with the measured numbers on the browser test's real-shaped script (top-only overshoot case added to the fixture or synthesized); the funscript browser suite green in the foreground; npm run check at zero; the plugin's twin (kinetic/bytes.js) untouched.
notes: Landed e74e3ef (main, unpushed). ui-pass formula not poured: one plugin feature on a single lane (Fable's call). fitMap replaces fitGain; map [lower, upper] via interp.map / mapOf; wideExtent and curveExtent return [min, max] (wideExtent now honors invert); INTERP.scaleAuto true, stored false stays (cleanInterp, no prefs.js change); readout 'bottom–top' (en dash, 'auto ' word dropped: 'auto 0.01..0.97' overflowed the 9ch cell by 45 px at 1280); overTip on the mode menu. fitMap keeps 1e-4 slack: the planner's e4/float32 noise read -0.000000 and pulled a 0.01 end (the old fitGain read 0.99 on PCHIP/Linear for the same reason). title: RFC-102: read the hub's fw_version as MAJOR.MINOR; hide what an older hub lacks; hub version once in About, never a dialog
description:
RFC-102 landed in Valence at 6a89df8 (SPEC §1.4, §4.2-5, §6.3, §12.6). The hub's identity `fw_version` is `MAJOR.MINOR` only; a client whose MINOR exceeds the hub's hides what the hub lacks and states the hub's version once in its about surface, never a warning dialog (operator ruling 2026-10-07).

What Phosphor implements:

1. Read identity `fw_version` as `MAJOR.MINOR`; a pre-RFC hub still sends `0.1.21-p4hub`, so take the first two numbers and ignore the rest.
2. When Phosphor's MINOR (the `tools/version.mjs` base) exceeds the hub's, hide the features the hub lacks and degrade nothing else. The gating list grows per feature as minors land; today it is empty, and sub-1.0 parties make no promise among themselves, so no gating on 0.y numbers.
3. The hub's version is stated once in the About surface (RENDERING §9 `utility` region), never a dialog. §12.6: a `fw_version` change SHOULD be surfaced ("this machine moved to X.Y"); the §12.6 gate on `configure` actions after a hub update stays MAY.
4. Phosphor's own version keeps RFC-102's mechanics already in place: `tools/version.mjs`, `npm run check`, CI stamping, `base/0.1`.

Open, not ruled (Valence follow-up bead): what HELLO `trust.client_ver` carries. The §12.6 tripwire compares the string; a full triple with PATCH moving every build trips it on every build.

description: Operator 2026-10-05: scrubbing the tape and stopping abruptly after a fast move overshoots the final position, then corrects. Two candidate causes, bench both. title: Factory plugin: funscript player with Stash support
description:
Factory widget plugin plugins/factory/funscript-player: plays a local or Stash video and drives the rail from its L0 funscript. Design: docs/plugins/FUNSCRIPT.md. Builder contract: plugins/factory/funscript-player/CONTRACT.md. Synthesized from three designs (sync, ux, protocol) by the judge, 2026-10-03.

SUMMARY
Media is the master clock: requestVideoFrameCallback presentation times map media time to performance.now() (median filter, 5 ms/s slew, 40 ms step re-anchor; currentTime fallback). The scheduler turns each funscript span into one segment {atMs execution start, norm, durationMs}, tiled from one mapping and sent once. It reaches the machine through ONE new host member, api.submitSegments(list): the host converts to hub time, subtracts the grant's schedule_latency_us (RFC-059), clips a late start keeping its end, takes what starts within HALF the granted horizon (RFC-087 keeps the RFC-014 SHOULD; registry max_future_schedule_ms note), packs 100 us t_off, and publishes on the segments STREAM found by role (0x2101 on valencesim, never named in code). Seek, rate, offset and transform changes are new superseding bundles (RFC-087 item 5); a stop is a short hold segment ending at rest, never PAUSE. Content goes as authored: end velocity unspecified, no curve_family, no client feasibility (SPEC 9.6 clauses 2, 4, 5). Safety gates ride the existing api.gate(field), extended to the c2h motion-input field: link, tier, latch, generator running, rail owned by another session, another plugin producing. Never auto-resumes. The card is a DAW-style arrangement: video stage, overview heat with scrub, an automation detail view (intent curve, measured reality trace), a fixed transport (Play, time, Motion, Offset, Invert, speed meter, volume) and one status slot; nothing shifts. Stash rides api.net.fetch (shell tauri-plugin-http) with GraphQL findScenes; every Stash fact is a marked assumption.

DECISIONS (veto-able; full reasons in FUNSCRIPT.md)
D1 Segments only, one new host door; the hero requires input.target + input.duration and declines elsewhere. No samples fallback.
D2 Lookahead = half the granted horizon, enforced in the host. The player offers up to 32; the host returns how many it consumed.
D3 The host owns time: atMs is an absolute performance.now() execution start; stamp = exec - schedule_latency_us. submitMotion's now+latency stamp is flagged for its owner, not changed here.
D4 As authored: end velocity unspecified, no curve_family. Stop-start at same-direction knots, if the live test shows it, is a Nucleus bead; client PCHIP end velocities are the veto alternative.
D5 rVFC media clock with median, slew and step (design 1).
D6 One mapping, segments tile, each sent once; restart supersedes.
D7 Stop = hold along the script min(200 ms, next action), at rest. Preroll on Play when the machine sits more than 5 % of the stroke from the script.
D8 Gates via api.gate on the segments field; a gate mid-play pauses the video; never auto-resume.
D9 One motion producer per session (host lock until the last sent segment ends + 500 ms).
D10 Offset (+-500 ms, 5 ms; zero = declared latency), Range (share of the hub window) and Invert are client content transforms; the window is never written; no intent permission.
D11 Speed meter and heat against limit.input.speed are display only.
D12 Dense scripts are thinned only after RATE_EXCEEDED, at the grant rate, extrema kept.
D13 Stash: direct stream only, Boolean interactive filter (assumption A3), no transcodes in v1.
D17 PUSHING BACK on the computed task: permissions are motion + net.fetch, not intent (the player writes no field); the manifest gets no panes key (the schema has none).
D18 Hub clock-offset filtering is deferred to a measurement on the P4; a fix belongs in Valence clients/js syncClock.
D19 No releaseMotion: PUBLISH rate 0 does not release the source (measured on valencesim).

OPERATOR RULINGS NEEDED BEFORE THE HOST LANDS THEM
R-A CANON FLAG: api.net.fetch (permission net.fetch) against DESIGN 2 'no HTTP backdoors'. Refuses the hub's own origins. No Stash without it.
R-B CSP: media-src 'self' blob: http: https: (blob: alone is needed for local files), img-src + http: https:; http capability + https://**.
R-C CANON FLAG: multi-module factory plugin against PLUGINS.md 'manifest plus one module'; an override copy must be bundled into one file.
R-D Permissions: motion + net.fetch, no intent (pushback above).

PROTOCOL GAPS (Valence RFC drafts owed, not built)
G1 A stream source stays owned until the session ends; no release intent is registered (SPEC 11.4 names one). Measured: jog refused SOURCE_CONFLICT after playback; PUBLISH rate 0 releases nothing.
G2 Stream vs generator exclusion is not enforced on Nucleus (an Advanced start and a segments bundle were both accepted, design 2 measurement); the player self-gates on pattern.running / advgen.running.

title: Layout switching: no position transitions, unsaved-changes prompt before switch, JSON export/import from the Layout menu
close_reason: Landed c3d52e9; decisions (incl. the autosave pushback) veto-able in the comment; builder-edit layouts + grid-model export green

comments.author: AtlanticTM
comments.text: Landed c3d52e9. VETO-ABLE: (1) PUSHBACK, recorded: layouts autosave on every edit (since ph-e82.3), so there are no literally unsaved changes and a plain 'unsaved changes?' prompt would be noise. The guard instead asks about changes SINCE EDITING BEGAN (or since the layout became active while editing): switching then shows an inline bar, not a modal (layout is not a hazard; ConfirmLayer stays for hazard prompts): Keep and switch / Discard and switch / Stay. Discard puts the layout back to that baseline (one undo step). Outside edit mode a switch never asks (the only writes there are nest folds). If you want explicit-save semantics instead (edits staged until Save), that is a larger change: say so. (2) No motion: the grid has no transition or animation on position, size or reflow, and the test asserts document.getAnimations() and transition-duration are empty/zero on the grid right after a switch (webui.md has no position-animation rule; law 12 reduced motion and 'nothing that could mislead' are the reasons). The dragged card's lift is a static offset. (3) Export/import live in the Layout menu (edit mode), shaped like the SettingsPane prefs backup: a textarea plus Export (fills it and copies to the clipboard) and Import. JSON is {app: 'phosphor', layout: name, views: {'<class>.<view>': placement map}}; modules are NOT included (a nest carries its own members). Import validates, keeps only object maps keyed class.view, never overwrites (a taken name becomes 'Name 2', 'Name 3'), a missing or prototype name becomes 'Imported', and refusals are named in words. Import then switches to it through the same guard. The prefs backup already carries phosphor.layouts whole, so the two stay consistent. Evidence: grid-model export block; builder-edit layouts block (guard bar, Stay keeps the change, Discard restores and switches, no animation or transition, a clean switch goes at once, Export JSON, Import as Default 2 and switched, foreign text refused). Regression note: responsive-matrix phone edit-mode rows still FAIL only from the sibling's uncommitted TopStrip.svelte (.measure/.home-btn reach 414 px); the open Layout menu itself measures 0..293 px at 360.

title: Density: compact mode token per layout and a per-card hide-label option for self-describing controls
close_reason: Landed e9b8ec8; decisions veto-able in the comment; builder-edit density + grid-model density green

comments.author: AtlanticTM
comments.text: Landed e9b8ec8. VETO-ABLE: (1) Density is a per-LAYOUT option (store.layouts[name].opts = {density}), two steps: comfortable (default, stored as no option) and compact. Toggled by a 'Compact cards in <layout>' switch in the Layout menu; it is an edit like any other (undoable, and it counts as a change for the switch guard). It travels with Save as, Rename, Export/Import, and the prefs backup. (2) Compact changes tokens, not cells: the cell edge (DESIGN §10.5, device px) is untouched; the gutter goes 7 -> 4 px (outline offset 4 -> 2 so neighbors' outlines stay apart), card body padding --gap -> 6 px, card label .8rem -> .7rem (11.2 px, above the matrix's 11 px floor). Handles keep max(40 px, --tap) (law 12). Nested grids inherit the top grid's density. (3) Hide label: per CARD (placement), stored as look.label = false beside the presentation, so it survives drags, duplicates and nests like any look. Offered only where the control names itself: every single field (Field draws its own label) and the safety ops (the button says E-Stop/Halt/Pause). Composites, plugin widgets, summaries and nests keep their label (they cannot be shown to name themselves). In edit mode the head stays (dimmed title) so the card can be grabbed and the label brought back; outside edit mode the head is gone. The field's label, the four-state ladder and its text reason are untouched (law 5). Evidence: grid-model density block (default, set, refuse unknown, invisible to placement, save as, export/import, reload, corrupt); builder-edit density block (stored on the layout, gutter and label shrink, label >= 11 px, handles >= 40 px, another layout stays comfortable, Label offered on the slider not on the pattern composite, look.label stored, head kept in edit, gone outside with the field label present, shown again clears it).

title: Multi-select in edit mode (shift-click, marquee): group move and delete, duplicate a card or nest, align and distribute
close_reason: Landed fd71c66; decisions veto-able in the comment; builder-edit select + grid-model selection green

comments.author: AtlanticTM
comments.text: Landed fd71c66. VETO-ABLE: (1) Selecting: a click on a card's GRIP selects it alone (a second click clears), Shift/Ctrl/Cmd+click adds or drops; keyboard Space on a focused grip does the same (aria-pressed carries the state). A click after a real drag is not a selection. A pointer drag across EMPTY grid draws a marquee and selects every card it crosses (Shift adds); a click on empty grid clears. Fine pointer only: no touch-action change, so a touch on empty grid still scrolls the page. Selection is per grid (a nest's members select within the nest), edit mode only, cleared on Done. (2) The edit hint line is replaced by a selection bar while anything is selected (no layout shift beyond the hint's own row): N selected, Duplicate, Align left, Align top (2+), Spread (3+), Remove, Clear. The toolbar keeps one row. (3) Group move: dragging a selected card's grip moves the whole selection by the same cell delta, clamped as one at the grid edges; a group never joins or leaves a nest by drag (single cards only). (4) Align left/top move every selected card to the selection's smallest x/y; Spread keeps the outermost two and spaces the rest evenly in x order. Collisions resolve by pushing the later card down, never by overlap. (5) Duplicate: a NEST is copied whole (members, their places and looks) under the next nest id, titled '<title> copy', placed below. A CARD on the home becomes a second placement keyed '<key>#<n>' (n from 2), same control, own place and own look; the palette still counts the control once and its Remove takes every placement, while the card's own Remove and the group Remove take only that placement. Law 10 reading: the instance key is the stable id plus a user-made instance number, never an index into catalog order, and it never binds anything new. Category pages and nest members offer no card Duplicate (a control is placed once per map); Duplicate is disabled there with a tooltip. (6) Remove on the home deletes from the home (a nest with its members, except members another nest also holds); on a category page it ungroups a nest; inside a nest it steps the member out. One undo step for the group. Owed elsewhere: Field.svelte uses field.uid as the element id, so two placements of one control (Duplicate, or one control in two nests, possible since ph-e82.6) give duplicate DOM ids; filed separately (not this agent's file). Evidence: grid-model selection block; builder-edit select block (grip click + Shift, group drag, marquee, align left without overlap, nest and card duplicate, group remove keeping a shared member, one undo, Done clears); home, nest, a11y, responsive home+nest green.

title: Nest header: collapsible, inline title edit, scroll/fixed toggle, in-flight count visible collapsed, empty placeholder, save-as-module, module reinsert preview
close_reason: Landed 0a9ed08; decisions veto-able in the comment; nest.test collapsed count, builder-edit nest, grid-model fold green

comments.author: AtlanticTM
comments.text: Landed 0a9ed08. VETO-ABLE: (1) Collapse is a layout property (nest.collapsed in the stored nest, per layout and view), toggled by a chevron at the start of the nest bar that is there in and out of edit mode. A collapsed nest packs NEST_FOLD_H = 2 rows (its card head plus the bar; rows still grow to content) and keeps its stored height for the unfold; things below rise. Members are unmounted while collapsed (their write state lives in the model, so nothing is lost). (2) Law 9 invariant: collapsing hides the members, NEVER the bar: the in-flight count stays drawn (nest.test asserts it on a held write). (3) The header IS the card head: in edit mode a nest's title is an inline input there (Enter or blur commits, Escape restores, an empty name is refused); the bar's separate name input is gone. (4) The bar holds, in order: fold, member count, in-flight count, then in edit mode: inert count, Add, Scrolling/Fixed (aria-pressed), Save module, Ungroup. Save module saves under the nest's title; a taken name is refused with 'rename the nest first' (no overwrite, no prompt). (5) Empty nest: 'Drop controls here' in edit mode, 'Empty nest' otherwise, drawn over the subgrid without taking its pointer events. (6) Module reinsert: choosing a module in the Layout menu previews its members before Insert: titled when this view can draw them, else the stored key marked '(not available here)', plus 'N of M available here; the rest stay inert until a catalog has them'. Insert is the confirmation and announces the same count. On the home 'available' means the catalog has it (Home resolves through its module list); on a category page it means the page draws it. Evidence: grid-model fold block; nest.test (collapsed hides members, keeps '1 in flight', expand redraws); builder-edit nest block (placeholder, inline title Enter/Escape, scroll toggle, fold packs 2 rows keeping h=6, preview lists the inert key, counts 1 of 2, preview writes nothing, Insert draws the live member and keeps the inert one); home, a11y, responsive home+nest green.

title: Keyboard: arrow nudge, shift-arrow resize, reading-order Tab, Enter opens the look picker, Delete removes, Escape cancels a drag
close_reason: Landed 6db3fc6; decisions veto-able in the comment; builder-edit keys + grid-model nudge green

comments.author: AtlanticTM
comments.text: Landed 6db3fc6. VETO-ABLE: (1) Up/Down CHANGED meaning on the grid: they used to swap reading order (commitOrder, which could fling a card across columns); they now pass the nearest card above/below in the card's own columns (grid.js nudgePin), because with vertical compaction a one-cell vertical step is always undone. At the top/bottom of its columns nothing moves and the live region says so. Left/Right step one cell, clamped. Stacked (phone width) Up/Down still walk the reading order. Keyboard moves act on the focused card only, never the group (group move is pointer-only for now). (2) Focus stays on the moved grip: a keyed #each reorder drops focus from the moved node, so it is restored after the move. (3) Tab order = DOM order = reading order (y, then x); during a pointer drag the DOM order is frozen (from ph-e82.20.2) and resyncs on release. (4) Enter on a grip opens the card's presentation picker: Home wraps LookEditor in [data-look]; the grid focuses that select and calls showPicker() where it exists. A card with no choices says so. Enter no longer clicks the grip (Space still selects). (5) Delete or Backspace on a grip removes the card, or its whole selection when it is selected; Ctrl+Z restores. (6) Escape: a drag in flight (pointer move/resize, marquee, a member leaving its nest) is dropped with nothing written; otherwise, outside text fields and popovers, it clears the selection. Evidence: grid-model nudge block; builder-edit keys block (Up passes the card above, focus kept, top refusal said, Down, Right nudge, Shift+Right grow, Tab meets grips in reading order, Enter focuses the look select, Escape mid-drag removes the ghost and writes nothing, Delete then Ctrl+Z). title: Drag feedback: lifted card, live sibling reflow, drop rect, nest highlight on drop, drag a member out of a nest to the top level
close_reason: Landed eec589f; decisions veto-able in the comment; builder-edit drag + grid-model drag green

comments.author: AtlanticTM
comments.text: Landed eec589f. VETO-ABLE: (1) The drag preview is the COMPACTED result (grid.js settle, shared with commitPin): the dragged card and its siblings are drawn where the release leaves them, so dragging into empty space below shows the card risen to where gravity puts it, not under the pointer. Honest over literal. (2) The dragged card stays in its grid cell (no free-floating follow-the-pointer layer); it lifts by a shadow and a static 3 px offset, never a transition (law 12 reduced motion, and no motion that could mislead about position). (3) Into a nest: the hit test uses the committed layout, and while the pointer is over a nest the rest of the grid stops reflowing (otherwise the pin pushes the nest away from the pointer). The whole subgrid lights (dashed intent outline, tint) because a joining member flows at the nest's end, not at a cell; palette drags onto a nest light it the same way and no longer draw a cell rect inside it. Safety ops and nests are never offered to a nest (placeable). (4) Out of a nest: leaving the nest BODY's visible rect (not the inner grid's, which a scrolling nest hides) hands the card to the parent grid, which shows the landing rect; release writes the top-level position first, then nestOut (one undo step). (5) Fixed on the way: Out on the home used nestRemove, so a member placed into a nest from the palette (no top-level entry) vanished from the home; Out now uses nestOut (look and size kept, flows unplaced when it never had a top-level place). (6) Fixed on the way: a keyed #each reordering the dragged node dropped pointer capture and stranded the drag; DOM order is frozen while any drag is in flight, and lostpointercapture ends a drag. title: Factory plugin: Advanced Penetration GUI (RFC-068 substitute for generator-advanced)
design:
Factory plugin "Advanced Penetration": the first plugin shipped in the repo (plugins/factory/advanced-penetration/), installed and enabled by default in the shell, removable (disable) like any plugin, same v1 contract. Substitutes RENDERING 10 generator-advanced per RFC-068 (RENDERING 10.2): registerHero with replaces 'advanced-generator', require = pattern.running + advgen.master + the six base roles (RFC-081, the same essential set as roles.js ADVGEN_SPEC), optional source.background_run, advgen.mode, action.store; modulators (RFC-066 mod.* roles, entry key 20 mod_target) claimed as per-entry instances (min 0) and drawn under the base control each rides. advgen.mode is essential only when pattern.select is present (RENDERING 10): the claim cannot express a conditional, so mount throws and the host falls back (10.2 item 5).

fray-d reference (github.com/fray-d/OSSM-Lite @ d20afa5, read 2026-10-02):
- docs/preset.html (the web config GUI): Master Speed, Max Depth, Min Depth, In Speed, Out Speed, In Acceleration, Out Acceleration, in that order; each base control carries its modifier table in a collapsible <details> directly under its slider (Amplitude, To Min, At Min, To Max, At Max, Offset); presets: Load + list + Delete, name + Save; rename was a three-step load/save/delete (we have the rename op); presets never carry master speed or depths (safety).
- docs/play.html: in/out speed are percentages of master; accel low = smooth, high = robotic; master 0 holds position. Modifier amplitude locks the other modifier fields until set (100 = off on fray-d; RFC-066 flips it to mod.amount 0 = off).
- Software/src/ossm/advanced_penetration/advanced_penetration_structs.h: Modifier::getModification is the cycling trapezoid (in_step ramp, in_wait hold, out_step ramp back, out_wait rest, offset phase in steps), cycle = stroke pairs; depth modulation pulls toward the opposing depth, other controls toward 0.
- advanced_penetration_ui.h drawStroke/calculateStroke: the stroke picture is depth (y) over time (x), the in half and out half each as wide as its stroke time from speed and accel (trapezoid velocity profile, bezier easing ratio accelTime/totalTime), plus a dotted outline of the maximum modulated stroke; drawBars: the modifier preview is a bar per step of the cycle.

Control map: stroke picture (depth window band on the rail, in half and out half from speed/accel); Master; Depth window (depth_max, depth_min); In stroke (speed_in, accel_in); Out stroke (speed_out, accel_out); every modulator as a <details> under its target with amount, rise, hold, fall, rest, phase (+ shape select when present) and a static cycle preview from reported values (no live phase cursor: the hub reports no modulator phase, so a moving cursor would claim machine state nobody reported); run/stop + background_run + mode in the head; presets list via the store (RFC-070 store_id) with save/load/rename/delete through action.store (RFC-067).
acceptance_criteria: Factory plugin loads by default in the shell and can be disabled; substitutes generator-advanced only when every essential binding resolves, else the host renders the generic widget or settings-card; every write through api.write with the law 5 ladder, gray-with-reason, law 12 targets, no red; npm run check zero, npm test green, plugins.test covers factory loading and the substitution fallback; Playwright on the fake hub with the role-carrying fixture; live smoke against valencesim once it carries the roles.

title: RFC-077: survive live catalog growth (subscribe 0x0001, refetch in the background, CHANNEL_WITHDRAWN, placements of withdrawn channels)
description:
RFC-077 (Valence rfc-cou) ACCEPTED, operator ruling 2026-10-01 (comment 01:32): subscribing to catalog 0x0001 is a MUST for every client; a user-space change keeps readiness, the client refetches in the background and sends CATALOG_READY with the new etag; withdrawn grants get one unsolicited NACK CHANNEL_WITHDRAWN; appeared channels deliver nothing until subscribed; no base etag (degraded mode for pinned clients). Risk accepted: stale layouts are covered by the byte-identical core guarantee and law 10 inert keys.

Change: src/model/machine.svelte.js applies a new catalog etag without a reconnect or a full UI reset (shadow, pending writes and open confirms on unaffected channels survive), subscribes to appeared accessory channels the user has placed, and treats withdrawn channels' placements as missing (ties to ph-uoh's orphan rendering); CHANNEL_WITHDRAWN is shown once per channel, not as a refusal storm. The session-layer half (subscribe, refetch, CATALOG_READY) is Valence clients/js (rfc-58u).

Prove it: fixture-replay test: an etag change adds and removes a user-space channel mid-session with no reconnect and no lost pending write elsewhere; live smoke once Nucleus val-9u0.12 or valencesim grows its catalog.
close_reason: Landed in 45e56ae: second catalog adoption in one session = in-place rebuild (survivors keep samples/grants/shadows/confirms; vanished channels drop samples+grants so placements go inert; appeared channels subscribed via wishes.js regrow); 0x0001 wished at critical priority (never shed) whenever the hub declares it; changed 0x0001 snapshot mid-session -> background session.requestCatalog() while LIVE holds (TODO(rfc-58u)); CHANNEL_WITHDRAWN NACK logged once per channel, grant dropped. Tests: test/wishes.test.mjs fixture replay (one channel appears, one leaves: only the new one wished, only the gone one removed, survivors untouched; 0x0001 never shed). Shadow survival is structural (shadow.svelte.js is never reset on catalog), not node-tested. Live: subscriptions unchanged on valencesim (first-adoption path; grants as before). OWED: live growth smoke -- valencesim declares no 0x0001 and never grows (needs Nucleus val-9u0.12 or a sim growth step), and valence-js rfc-58u (until it lands the refetch adopts with verified=false and is not cached). VETO-ABLE: all appeared h2c channels are subscribed (the generic policy), not only placed ones.

title: RFC-087/059: timed motion sender fills segments bundles to the advertised horizon and leads media by schedule_latency_us
description:
RFC-087 (Valence rfc-66i), operator rulings 2026-10-01 (comments 01:06, 01:08), and RFC-059 (rfc-r4v) ACCEPTED (comment 00:28; clients SHOULD lead media by schedule_latency_us and MUST NOT hardcode it).

Change:
- Lookahead senders (TCode/funscript plugin input, any timed source) use the segments-kind STREAM and fill each bundle up to the hub-advertised horizon from the GRANT (250 default, 500 or 1000), up to 32 segments / 242 B. The horizon caps start stamps; each segment executes at its stamp. A low-latency sender stamps ~50 ms ahead in small bundles under the same horizon. Samples-kind keeps its 20 ms span.
- Media lead = the grant's schedule_latency_us; no hand-tuned offset anywhere in Phosphor.
- Seek/skip flush: use exactly the spelling the RFC-087 draft lands (pause then resume, or a dedicated flush op/seq rule).
- RFC-058 (rfc-zj1) is ACCEPTED: ph-vdk.35's routing of timed input to the segments STREAM is unblocked and lands with this bead.

Likely files: src/model/motion.js (createMotionDoor, FALLBACK_RATE_HZ), src/plugins/host.js, the TCode adapter path; Valence clients/js sender exposes both grant keys (rfc-cl6).

Prove it: unit test: bundles never exceed the advertised horizon or 32 segments; lead equals the fixture grant's schedule_latency_us; live smoke against valencesim and one bench pass with MultiFunPlayer TCode at horizon 250 and 1000 (ph-vdk.27's loader path).
close_reason: Landed in 08b839a: timed input -> segments STREAM {input.target, input.duration, end_velocity unspecified}, start = hub now + grant.scheduleLatencyUs (no constant), within grant.scheduleHorizonMs; bundleHead packs a timed list to horizon / 32 / min_transport_payload; per-channel grants; flush = RFC-087 item 5 supersede (each bundle replaces the unstarted tail, no separate op). Tests: plugins.test.mjs (e) segments routing, lead == fixture schedule_latency_us, bundles never pass horizon/32/payload at 250/500/1000. Live (valencesim): segments 0x2101 granted 50 Hz horizon 250 lead 1000 us; 11 timed inputs accepted, sync_bundles +11, sync_dropped 0. OWED: MultiFunPlayer TCode bench pass at horizon 250 and 1000 in the shell (sim grants only 250); a lookahead source (funscript) has no plugin API yet, bundleHead is ready for it. VETO-ABLE: lead is schedule_latency_us only, not RFC-087's illustrative 50 ms client lead; if real links show deadline_stretched anomalies, add the measured CLOCK rtt/2, still no hand-tuned constant.

title: RFC-062: document the renderer-class boundaries and enforce the derived floor as the desktop minimum window
description:
RFC-062 (Valence rfc-l8p) ACCEPTED, operator ruling 2026-10-01 (comment 01:01), open question 1: RENDERING 12.1 RECOMMENDS boundary values informatively in CSS px (handheld/full near 600 to 960, the client's choice stated) and defines the FLOOR by derivation: the width at which the persistent strip still holds its mandatory controls at law 12's 40 px targets. Below the floor no client degrades further; a desktop client MUST enforce the floor as its OS minimum window size (Phosphor: 320 today).

Change: state Phosphor's chosen boundaries (src/model/rclass.js GLANCE_DOWN 216 etc. and the handheld/full split) in docs/DESIGN.md with the RENDERING 12.1 pointer; derive the floor from the strip's mandatory controls (e-stop + pause after RFC-085, at 40 px) and set src-tauri/tauri.conf.json windows[0].minWidth to it (320 today; ph-vdk.40 tracks dropping it once sub-320 layout holds, so the two must agree with the derivation). The class switch keeps content, category, pending writes and open confirms (already the RFC's rule).

Prove it: test/renderer-class.test.mjs asserts the documented constants; test/shell-chrome-geometry.test.mjs asserts minWidth equals the derived floor; npm run check zero findings.

title: RFC-083: color and datetime archetypes by role (RGB; datetime in hub time converted with the CLOCK offset)
description:
RFC-083 (Valence rfc-vdc) ACCEPTED option B, operator ruling 2026-10-01 (comment 00:19): the archetype hint is struck; row 4 pad2d binds by identity, rows 16/17 (color, datetime) by role.

Change:
- color: bind color.red/green/blue (RGB only; no HSV role set exists, a hub converts in firmware). A picker writes the three fields as one intent.
- datetime: datetime.moment / datetime.start / datetime.end carry HUB TIME (seconds in the hub's section 7.1 timebase), never Unix epoch. Phosphor converts to wall time with the CLOCK offset it already holds, and back on write. A stored moment is valid for the hub's current boot_id: on a boot_id change the client marks it stale and re-arms (never silently shifts it).
- Remove any archetype-hint read from the settings model.

Likely files: src/model/settings.js (archetype projection), src/model/roles.js, src/ui/Field.svelte or new widgets, src/model/machine.svelte.js (CLOCK offset, boot_id).

Prove it: settings-model test: fixture fields with the roles project to color/datetime; datetime round trip through a fixed CLOCK offset is exact; a boot_id change marks the value stale; no hub emits these today, so fixtures only (state it on close).
close_reason: Landed in 549665b: archetype hint read removed; color.red/green/blue per group -> one color picker (writes coalesce into one intent on a shared write channel); datetime.* -> row 17 datetime-local over hub seconds via format.js hubSecToWallMs/wallMsToHubSec (CLOCK hub-us + telemetry.uptime wrap), disabled with a reason when no uptime; machine.link.bootId from WELCOME; a moment this page armed reads stale after a boot_id change and offers Re-arm (never shifted). Tests: settings-model.test.mjs (projection, partial/read-only triples decline, hint ignored, exact round trip through a fixed CLOCK ref, boot_id stale). FIXTURES ONLY: no hub emits color/datetime roles today (valencesim d49f36ed905e65bb has none); page smoke on the sim shows no regressions. VETO-ABLE: an interval (datetime.start+end) is two inputs in one group, not a dedicated range picker; staleness tracks only moments this page armed (in memory).

title: RFC-072: remove the mDNS _valence._tcp browse; UDP probe only; read the pinned BLE manufacturer-data layout
description:

title: DashGrid: nests read untracked while the view map is missing; announce region anchored to the viewport
description: Two grid-layer bugs found building the home (ph-e82.5). (1) dashboard.svelte.js read() is G.viewMap(..., false): when the view's map does not exist yet, grid.js own() checks a missing key on the layout proxy, which Svelte does not track, and returns a fresh plain {}. DashGrid's nests derived then never re-runs when the map is created, so New nest on a view the user never arranged stores the nest but draws nothing until remount. Root fix: read() also reads Object.keys(layouts.layouts[layouts.active]) (or viewMap tracks). Home.svelte works around it by creating its map in an effect.pre; category pages are still affected. (2) DashGrid's .sr-only announce div is position:absolute with no positioned ancestor, so its containing block is the initial containing block; as an abspos child of the flex .dash-wrap its static position is the grid's top. When anything above the grid pushes that below the fold (the home palette; HubPicker in a short window) the document grows, and scrolling it carries the top strip off screen (law 11; responsive-matrix stripCheck caught it at 1280x720). Root fix: .dash-wrap { position: relative }. Home.svelte contains it via .home { position: relative }.
close_reason: Fixed in 8a6d51f: grid.js own() reads the value first (subscribes to a missing key on a proxy); .dash-wrap position: relative; Home workarounds removed. Evidence: nest.test (New nest on a never-arranged view draws, failed before), responsive-matrix --only home (announce region contained, strip checks pass), grid-model, home.test.

title: buttplug fork: StopCmd ignores its device index; device index allocation races
description:
Found building ph-e82.8 part 2 (toys as modules). Both in ../ButtplugIO (branch valence), not Phosphor code.

1. ServerDeviceManager::stop_devices (crates/buttplug_server/src/device/server_device_manager.rs) stops EVERY device and ignores StopCmdV4's device_index/feature_index. StopDeviceCmd v0..v3 converts to StopCmd(Some(index)), so an Intiface app stopping one toy stops all of them. Phosphor's bp_toy_stop works around it by sending zero outputs (docs/BUTTPLUG.md, Toy stops).

2. DeviceConfigurationManager::device_index (crates/buttplug_server_device_config/src/device_config_manager.rs) computes a free index from user_device_definitions and inserts later, with no lock across connect tasks; two devices finishing their connection together get the same index and the second replaces the first in the device map (reproduced with three upstream simulated devices in one scan: one of the three never lists). Phosphor's cargo tests run one simulated toy per server for this reason.

Fix home is the fork (upstream PR candidate). Acceptance: a StopDeviceCmd for one device leaves another device's output untouched; N simulated devices found in one scan all list with distinct indices.
close_reason: Fixed in the fork, branch valence: 36110484 (StopCmd with a device index stops only that device; unknown index is DeviceNotAvailable; no index still stops all) and b898a4d1 (device index allocated atomically with its insert). Phosphor 185bc64: bp_toy_stop is StopCmd(Some(index), outputs only) and the cargo toy tests run three simulated toys plus the machine in one scan, 13/13 passed on ten runs.
