comments.text: Fixed in ButtplugIO branch valence (not pushed). 36110484 fix(server): StopCmd with a device index stops only that device (server_device_manager.rs:298 stop_devices ignored the index; unknown index now DeviceNotAvailable; StopCmd without index still stops all; feature_index is still ignored by DeviceHandle::handle_stop_device_cmd). b898a4d1 fix(device-config): new device index allocated atomically with its insert (device_config_manager.rs:389/:416, a Mutex across lookup, allocation and insert). Tests in buttplug_tests/tests/test_simulated_devices.rs: test_simulated_stop_one_device_leaves_other_running (failed before, passes) and test_simulated_devices_found_together_get_distinct_indices (3 simulated devices in one scan on a 4-worker multi-thread runtime, 10 rounds per run; failed 3/3 before, 10/10 runs pass after). The race only shows on a multi-thread runtime, which Tauri and Phosphor's #[tokio::test(flavor = multi_thread)] tests use. Phosphor workarounds: both can be removed. src-tauri path-depends on the fork working tree, so the fixes are already live. bp_toy_stop / Buttplug::toy_stop can send StopCmdV4::new(Some(index), None, false, true) (outputs only, write-acknowledged, uses the device's own stop set) instead of per-feature zero OutputCmds; pass inputs=true only if a toy stop should also drop sensor subscriptions. The one-simulated-toy-per-server restriction in the cargo tests can go. docs/BUTTPLUG.md 'Toy stops' needs the matching update.

title: A stale intent's late rejection clobbers a newer write on the same shadow record
description:
shadow.svelte.js flush(): when an INTENT gets no answer, the shadow's own FAULT_MS (2 s) timer faults the record first ('no echo'); the session's sendIntent timeout (3 s, session.js) then rejects the same promise and flush's catch calls fail() on whatever the record holds NOW. If the operator wrote again in that 1 s window, the newer write is marked fault ('refused: Error'), its requested value discarded, and lastRefusal updated, although that newer write is still in flight and may yet confirm. Transient ground-truth defect (law 4/5): the control states a refusal the hub never made. Seen in test/control-contract.test.mjs (it now sleeps 1.2 s after its silent-hub step to keep runs independent).

Fix sketch: tag each shadow record with the send it belongs to (sentAt or an intent counter captured in flush) and ignore a settle/fail from an older send.

TEST/VALIDATION PLAN: control-contract silent step without the drain sleep: write, wait for fault, write again within 1 s, assert the second write is pending (not fault) until its own echo.
acceptance_criteria: A late rejection never changes a record that a newer write owns; control-contract passes without the drain sleep.
close_reason: Acceptance met: test/control-contract.test.mjs drops the drain sleep and checks a newer write survives the silent intent's late timeout (fails x3 on pre-8f66ce0 shadow, passes on HEAD). Fix 8f66ce0, test 5c03422.

Proven: a scratch copy of test/control-contract.test.mjs with the 1.2 s drain sleep replaced by 'write again in hold mode while the old intent's session timeout lands; after 1.3 s the newer write is still pending/overdue; release; it confirms' FAILS on the previous shadow.svelte.js (fault x3 presentations) and PASSES with the fix. title: Builder (g): embed buttplug in the shell as an Intiface-compatible server; machine via the intent path, toys as modules
description:
Phase (g), DESIGN §10.8. Embed a buttplug server in the Tauri shell (Rust crates from ../buttplug: buttplug_server, buttplug_server_device_config, the btleplug/serial/hid hardware managers, a websocket server connector) speaking the Intiface-compatible server protocol, so games and apps built for Intiface Central connect to Phosphor. The machine is a buttplug device whose commands enter the kernel intent path (host.js submitMotion, the TCode adapter's door, motion permission), never a second Valence session; the fork's buttplug_server_hwmgr_slopsync (own WS session, mDNS) is NOT linked. Toys found by the hardware managers appear as modules (phase c contract) and as relationship targets (see the relationship CANON FLAG in DESIGN §10.8). Listener binds loopback by default; LAN exposure waits on ph-vdk.28. Desktop first; Android is its own later question.

TEST/VALIDATION PLAN:
- cargo test in src-tauri for the device-to-intent bridge: a LinearCmd maps to one submitMotion call with the same 0..1 position and duration as the TCode adapter's mapping for the same input.
- Loopback client test (buttplug's client crate, or a JSON fixture over ws://127.0.0.1): handshake, RequestDeviceList returns the machine, a LinearCmd reaches the fake kernel.
- Against valencesim: a buttplug client drives the machine; a second raw Valence session sees the motion, and the hub reports exactly one session from Phosphor.
- By hand: a real Intiface-targeting app connects with no change beyond the port; a BLE toy appears as a module; the strip e-stop halts the machine while the buttplug client keeps sending.

Intiface-class server UI landed (operator direction 2026-10-02). Phosphor d67090f (settings), ec29760 (devices), 1f937d0 (machine Vibrate, ph-e82.13.4), 9f09eae (clients), a304f15 (log), 2a8e7e3 (status row). New event bp://clients; bp://log gains time; bp_devices gains protocol, address, device_name, display_name and lists remembered (connected:false) devices. All in docs/BUTTPLUG.md. ServerPane stays self-contained (no props, exports nothing new); tabs live in src/shell/server/*.

VETO-ABLE DECISIONS (each reversible on a word):
1. Settings persist Rust-side as settings.json in the app config dir (buttplug/), not localStorage: start-on-launch then runs from Rust setup whether or not any pane is mounted (the drawer may mount it lazily), and the device config already lives Rust-side.
2. The port and the hardware managers are refused while the server runs (Intiface Central locks them too), so saved settings always describe the running server. Log level and start-on-launch apply at once.
3. "Allow raw messages" NOT offered (pushback): the fork speaks spec v4 and implements no raw read/write commands in any spec version, so the setting would drive nothing (webui.md: a control that drives nothing is a defect). The settings tab says so in one line.
4. Upstream buttplug log lines reach bp://log only where Phosphor owns the process logger (release builds); in debug builds tauri-plugin-log owns it and they go to the dev console. Moving that would mean editing lib.rs setup beyond registration lines.
5. The device config is upstream's user device config file (devices.json, save_user_config/load_protocol_configs), saved on every device-list change and every rename/forget, write-then-rename under one lock. Rename applies to bp_devices at once; connected apps see it from the toy's next connection (upstream copies the name at connect).
6. The machine refuses rename, disconnect and forget: its identity is documented as fixed and it comes and goes with the hub link.
7. Forget is refused while connected; remembered devices (connected:false) are listed after connected ones so they can be forgotten.
8. The pane's scan is timed at 30 s (SCAN_S) and stops itself unless another scan request comes first; Rust takes any seconds or none.
9. Scan state now flips where the scan is requested (Buttplug::scan), not in the machine manager, so it shows with the machine manager off.
10. Clients: one at a time as before (Intiface parity); message rate is counted per whole second server-side; connected-since is the server host's clock. bp://clients emits at most 1 Hz while name or rate changes.
11. Log: 500 lines kept, level filter is view-only, copy is plain text with ISO times; the latest error line shows under the status row until the next start request.
12. Hit targets are 40 px for every pane control (law 12), up from 36 px on fine pointers.
13. tokio "time" is named in src-tauri/Cargo.toml (outside the listed ownership; one word) for the scan timer and the client rate tick.
14. Machine Vibrate: Vibrate only, 0..100 steps; Rotate not added (no consumer asked). bp_toy_* still refuse the machine.

TESTS: cargo test 13/13 (new: settings_persist_and_gate_the_managers, device_config_rename_disconnect_forget, timed_scan_stops_itself, clients_list_rate_and_operator_disconnect; loopback and stop-all extended for the machine Vibrate); fork cargo test -p buttplug_server valence 2/2, -p buttplug_transport_websocket_tungstenite 2/2; npm run check and npm test green; test/server-pane.test.mjs covers every new command path with a fake invoke/listen.

No live check of the UI geometry inside the sibling's drawer.

title: Builder (e): nests (scrolling or fixed subgrids) and saveable nests
description:
Phase (e), DESIGN §10.6. A nest is a control holding a subgrid, scrolling or fixed by the user's choice. A nest with its contents is saveable as a reusable module, stored with the layouts, keyed on roles or uids (law 10). Placing a saved nest on a machine that lacks some bindings leaves those members inert, never an error. A scrolling nest must not hide pending or degraded state (RENDERING §9 invariant): its frame shows the in-flight count, as drillCard does in App.svelte today. The placement rule for single fields (anywhere vs nests-only) comes from the rulings bead.

TEST/VALIDATION PLAN:
- test/grid-model.test.mjs: nest serialize/deserialize round trip; a saved nest reinserted under a different catalog keeps inert members and survives another round trip.
- Playwright on the fake-hub harness: a pending write inside a scrolled-away region of a scrolling nest shows on the nest frame; the count clears on echo.
- test/responsive-matrix.mjs: a nested scroll never traps page scroll on phone viewports.
acceptance_criteria: Nests hold subgrids, save as reusable modules, reinsert on another catalog with inert members; a pending write inside a nest is visible on its frame.

comments.author: AtlanticTM
comments.text:
2026-10-01 landed (see commit). Decisions recorded as VETO-ABLE:
1. ph-e82.1 item 4 (single fields anywhere vs nests-only) stays OPEN. Coded both ways behind FIELDS_NESTS_ONLY in src/model/grid.js (default false = anywhere); placeable(kind, inNest, nestsOnly) is the one rule the palette and DashGrid read. Flip the constant to rule nests-only.
2. Storage: a nest is an entry in its view's placement map, id nest:<n> (client-made, never wire vocabulary, law 10), carrying {title, scroll, map}; the member map's keys ARE the membership, null = not yet placed. Members the catalog lacks stay inert: never drawn, never deleted, counted in edit mode only ("N not on this machine").
3. Modules (saved nests) live in the same phosphor.layouts store under `modules`, shared by every layout, class and view, keyed on the members' stable ids. A taken module name is refused, never silently overwritten.
4. An item that is a member of any nest is drawn inside it, never also at the top level; one control may sit in two nests (a module inserted twice). Nests never nest.
5. The frame count mirrors drillCard: every member field not confirmed (pending, overdue, fault) counts, on every nest (not only scrolling ones), in a bar outside the scroll region that is always drawn so the count never shifts layout (law 5).
6. Stacked (<= 640 CSS px) a nest never scrolls by itself, so it cannot trap the page scroll; ph-e82.7 may revisit.
7. Reset layout forgets positions only: nests keep size and members and reflow. Ungroup returns present members to the top level and discards the nest's inert members with it.
8. Nests render on every DashGrid view, including the derived category pages (arrangement only; every field stays reachable). If the home should be the only nest surface, gate it in App, not grid.js.
Root-cause fix found on the way: a key deleted from a Svelte $state proxy still answers hasOwnProperty (svelte 5.56 deleteProperty never deletes from the target), so grid.js own() lied after any delete: a member moved out could not be added back, and switchLayout to a deleted layout name would succeed and then crash viewMap. own() now also requires a defined value; grid-model covers it.
Tests: grid-model (nest round trip, reinsertion under a different catalog keeping inert members, second round trip, flag both ways, the proxy ghost); test/nest.test.mjs (check:nest, in test:browser) on the fake hub: a held write on a scrolled-away member shows "1 in flight" on the frame outside the scroll region, clears on echo, plus the edit flow (ungroup, new, add, save module, out, re-add, insert); responsive-matrix `nest` scenario at 320/360/390: no nested scroll region, a wheel over the nest scrolls the page, phone checks pass.

title: Plugin motion input rides command.position; move it to the motion-segment STREAM once clients/js can publish
description: STATE (2026-09-25, plugin surface landed): shadow.svelte.js submitMotion() maps a normalized input onto the stroke window (model/motion.js) and sends it as a command.position setpoint via sendCommand. durationMs (TCode I<ms>) is accepted and DROPPED, and the hub plans it as a manual point move at USER ceilings, not the input limit set. RFC-044 names segments/samples as the translation. BLOCKER: Valence clients/js sends no publish wishes (HELLO key 11) and has no STREAM sender (session.js buildHello comment), and Valence is read-only from here. ACCEPTANCE: submitMotion emits {target, duration} on the catalog's segments-kind STREAM (by stream kind, never by id) with the granted publish; command.position stays only as the fallback for hubs with no stream channel. Verified: node test/plugins.test.mjs covers the mapping only, never a live hub.
notes: Landed 0a4e670. Router: src/model/motion.js createMotionDoor/motionStream; shadow.svelte.js submitMotion delegates. ACCEPTANCE RE-SCOPED by the orchestrator dispatch 2026-09-25: samples-kind STREAM (not the segments-kind one this bead names). Why segments stays open: encodePacked needs every layout field, and an absent end velocity has no spec encoding (RFC-058 / RFC-071 OQ1); a 0 means end-at-rest on Nucleus 0x2101 (catalog comment, -32768 is its sentinel), so zero-fill would stop at every knot of a dense stream. Follow-up filed. Grant: LAZY on first submitMotion (a watch-only session reserves no publish slot; a cold HELLO has no catalog to pick the channel by kind). Duration: samples t_base = hubNow + durationMs, capped at max_future_schedule_ms (SPEC 5.4: a samples timestamp is the instant described). SPEC GAP, noted here not in RFC-071 (not a roles question): 5.4 states no lead cap for samples-kind, while Nucleus clamps samples to 250 ms and plans a future-anchored bare point as a scheduled START (kinetic.hpp commit), not an arrival, so the lead delays chase by the duration on that hub. title: Draft the Phosphor-discovered spec gaps into Valence RFC-QUEUE
description:
MISSING: Phosphor hits several places where Valence is silent or self-contradictory. Per doctrine, code does not bind to an unaccepted clause; these need RFC drafts in Valence spec/RFC-QUEUE.md (the one writable door), then rulings, then the Phosphor beads that depend on them.

THE LIST (details in the epic report):
1. Live renderer-class selection for a resizable viewport (RENDERING §12 silent beyond "adopts the nearer one").
2. The `destructive` flag referenced by RENDERING §8.2 row 6 / §8.4 / registry ui_archetypes has no wire carrier (SPEC §8.8 setting_flags has no such bit).
3. RENDERING §8.4 `select` says index 0 is filler for every select; SPEC §8.9 (line 738) limits that to action.* op tables. Contradiction.
4. Identifying a device-authored anomaly/event channel and labeling its event kinds (SPEC line 1388 deferred it; Phosphor currently regexes names).
5. Advanced-generator lane count: RENDERING §2.2 says four lanes; Nucleus emits six. Make the lane count catalog-declared.
6. `action.preset` (Nucleus) is not a registered action tag (registry has preset_save/preset_recall).
7. Tier-2 substituted-widget conformance (RENDERING §10/§13 silent) - co-own with the plugin-surface agent.
8. Client-pushed provisioning of a fresh hub (RFC-054 frames only hub-disclosure).

ACCEPTANCE: each item is either an RFC-QUEUE draft or a recorded decision that no RFC is needed; the Phosphor beads that depend on one link to it.
notes: Drafted 2026-09-25 in Valence spec/RFC-QUEUE.md (commits 9f6ee9d..0199b2d), one rfc- bead each on the Valence board: (1) renderer-class selection RFC-062 rfc-l8p [ph-vdk.5]; (2) destructive flag carrier RFC-063 rfc-c5u [ph-vdk.4, ph-vdk.3]; (3) index-0 filler scope RFC-064 rfc-8pk [ph-vdk.3]; (4) event purpose roles + kind labels RFC-065 rfc-x3n [ph-vdk.7, ph-vdk.14]; (5) advanced-generator lanes RFC-066 rfc-0sm [ph-vdk.11]; (6) action.preset -> registered action.store op select RFC-067 rfc-2n5 [ph-vdk.11, ph-vdk.3]; (7) substituted-widget conformance RFC-068 rfc-8qh (cross-refs RFC-061, the TCode-adapter plugin entry another agent drafted the same day, still uncommitted at close); (8) client-pushed WiFi provisioning RFC-069 rfc-qf5 [ph-vdk.24]. All DRAFT, rulings pending. Dependent Phosphor beads should not bind to these clauses until accepted.
close_reason: Eight RFC drafts landed in Valence RFC-QUEUE (RFC-062..069), beads rfc-l8p/c5u/8pk/x3n/0sm/2n5/8qh/qf5

title: axis-hero binding set is looser than law 7: the rail claims with only window.min/max
description:

title: Keyboard and accessibility basics: tablist roving, user text size, reactive reduced motion
description:
MISSING: both nav tablists (rail and phone strip) and the LogPane tabs lack arrow-key roving focus and aria-controls/tabpanel wiring. The root font-size is a pixel value, so the operator's browser/OS text-size preference has no effect (it also means a 4K display at 100% scaling gets 18px text in a 1680px column). Several labels sit at .56-.62rem (~10px). Two components read prefers-reduced-motion once at module load and ignore later changes.

EVIDENCE: App.svelte:321-335 and :349-354, LogPane.svelte:118-124, style.css:164 (`font-size: calc(var(--s) * 16px)`), style.css:506 (.app max-width 1680px), SafetyBar.svelte chip labels (.56-.62rem), LinkBar.svelte chip (.62rem), RailWidget.svelte:332-333, LinkBar.svelte:148-149. RENDERING.md §13 law 12 (reduced motion is a floor), §8.3 full class ("keyboard-typeable").

Roving tabindex + Arrow-key nav on both tablists (rail vertical, phone strip horizontal), Tab leaves in one step. rail-collapse gets aria-label. html font-size moved from calc(--s*16px) to calc(--s*100%) (style.css) so the browser's own text-size default is honored, --s still multiplies on top -- verified 22.40px at a 20px default via CDP Page.setFontSizes, no overflow at 360/1280w. Added a :focus-visible ring on the range slider thumb (style.css), the one control whose outline:none had no visible replacement. Dropped role=tabpanel/aria-controls wiring: <main> is a landmark per this codebase's own rule and Svelte's a11y linter correctly rejected an interactive role on it; roving focus is the literal scope asked for. Tests: test/a11y-basics.test.mjs (24 checks, all pass), wired into npm run test:browser. responsive-matrix stays at 0 findings; shell-chrome-geometry unaffected.

title: Display latency: telemetry->numeral is +140 ms (measured); cut it (higher grant rate, smaller LEAD_MS/render delay) and measure the Tauri shell separately
description: Measured 2026-09-21 against Nucleus 88fd666 in Chromium (Vite dev): hub +20 ms, Phosphor +140 ms, end to end +160 ms, corr 0.98, amplitude preserved. telebuf.js LEAD_MS 30 / MAX_LEAD_MS 150 and createRenderClock delay clamp(20..120, p95_gap*1.5+frameDt) were sized for the S3's clumpy 25 Hz arrivals; the P4 delivers every 35 ms with p95 40 ms, so the same arithmetic gives ~29 ms at a 60 Hz grant (machine.svelte.js TELEMETRY_HZ=25 is a measured choice for the S3, re-measure). Also measure inside phosphor.exe (WebView2), which the operator uses; the instrument is Nucleus/tools/lag_probe.py --dump plus a rAF sampler of .hn-val.mono. Never trade truth for smoothness: T18 (arrival stamping) still binds.
close_reason: Wire-to-numeral 82->22 ms (Chromium), 63->19 ms (shell WebView2), at the floor of half the arrival period plus a frame; numerals show the newest sample, the rail keeps its render delay (5728d12)

comments.author: AtlanticTM
comments.text: Code side (sha in next comment): the dominant client term was not LEAD_MS or the render delay but a RATCHET in telebuf push(): ts = max(arrival+lead, prev+EMA period) only ever moves forward, so EMA noise walks the schedule up to MAX_LEAD_MS (150) and it stays there; the cap then stores arrival+150, i.e. arrival stamping with an offset (T18). Sim (test/telebuf-sim.mjs, P4-like 35-45 ms arrivals): display lag p95 187 ms before, 93 ms after. Changes: respace at 0.98 x EMA period (SCHEDULE_PERIOD_TRIM) so the walk drifts down to the arrival floor; SCHEDULE_MAX_LEAD_MS 150->60; LEAD_MS 30 removed (redundant with the render delay, which already sizes to 1.5 x p95 gap + a frame); RENDER_DELAY_MIN/MAX_MS named, values unchanged (20/120); TELEMETRY_HZ 25->50 (four 5 ms pacer ticks, under the motion channel's 60 Hz max_rate_hz; SPEC 6.7 refuses per wish only on channel/access/count, SPEC 10.2 clamps to max_rate_hz, so never a refused rate; 60 Hz truncates to 16 ms and the tick rounds it to 20, i.e. 50 Hz under a 60 Hz grant). Sim predicts ~55-70 ms client lag at 50 Hz. title: Rust shell: UDP discovery magic/port were re-pinned to the Valence registry
description:
src-tauri/src/discovery.rs is a HAND-TRANSCRIBED copy of registry udp_discovery. At carve-out it still held the pre-rename values (port 21328, magic 'SLOP'); the registry now pins port 22096 and magic 'VLNC' (0x56 0x4C 0x4E 0x43). Changed here to match the registry, which is the one home (C-1).

Consequence, operator-veto-able: this shell can no longer discover a hub still speaking the old magic/port, which is every build of the archived S3 firmware. Verify against ValenceDrive once its discovery side is re-pinned too.

The old repo checked this by tools/spec-drift.sh, which did not come across. Either port that check here or accept the hand copy as unguarded (T20 says an unguarded hand copy drifts silently).
notes: Inventoried every registry-derived constant hand-copied in Phosphor outside the imported Valence JS client: discovery.rs PORT/MAGIC (already re-pinned, matched), ble-ws.js BLE_SERVICE/CHAR_C2H_WRITE/CHAR_H2C_NOTIFY (still pre-rename SLOP/SYNC UUIDs, drifted), ShellBar.svelte DISCOVERY_PORT (still 21328, drifted). No frame-type literals (0x1E/0x1F), ws_subprotocol, or mdns_service are hand-spelled anywhere in src/ or src-tauri/. Wrote test/check-registry-pins.mjs: parses registry.yaml's udp_discovery and ble_identity blocks with a small line-oriented scalar parser (no yaml dep) and greps the 2 Rust + 3 JS pins for a match, failing with file:line and both values. Rust cannot import JS so it stays gated by this script permanently (stated in the file banner); ws_subprotocol/mdns_service are already codegen-emitted and nothing in Phosphor spells them, so nothing to convert to an import. Fixed the 2 drifted files to match the registry (same C-1 precedent as this bead's own discovery.rs fix): ble-ws.js UUIDs 534c4f50-5359-4e43-... -> 56414c45-4e43-4531-..., ShellBar.svelte DISCOVERY_PORT 21328 -> 22096. Wired into npm run check (also added check:pins). npm run check: all green (device-knowledge, registry-pins, settings-model). cargo check in src-tauri: Finished dev profile, zero errors/warnings.
close_reason: Staleness gate landed (test/check-registry-pins.mjs, wired into npm run check) and the two drifted hand-copies it found (ble-ws.js BLE UUIDs, ShellBar.svelte DISCOVERY_PORT) were fixed to match the registry. Rust pins have no import escape and stay gated by the script; check green, cargo check clean.

title: Open funscript analyzer at rest: a change on a Tuning channel waits for the next frame, which nothing schedules while no claimed field moves
description: Pre-existing (main 278c28b too), seen while making ph-uve3 exact: the open analyzer reads on the frame after api.changed moves, but at rest a frame comes only from a claimed field's update (PluginSlot's watch), the player's own loop or an input. Nucleus pushes position, window and speed only on change, so with the machine parked another client's write to a Tuning channel (or a mask change there) moves the sequence and waits for whatever frame comes next, possibly long after. api.changed is pull-only. Options: PluginSlot also watches the channels a plugin names (an api to declare them), or api.onChanged(channels, fn) that kicks the plugin's frame; either keeps zero per-frame reads.
close_reason: lp/perf4 069d253 (unmerged, on main 0321350). api.onChanged(channelsOrRoles, fn), experimental (PLUGINS.md): src/model/changes.js watchers, told on a microtask after a move they accept (or bumpAll), then at most once a frame while moves keep coming; idle nothing runs per frame. Roles resolve at each move; host.js guards fn, keeps the unsubscribe on the plugin's closers (dropped on deactivation, taken off on unsubscribe); not told of the motion lock's lapse. The analyzer watches the channels it reads with onRender, renews per catalog, drops on unmount. Tests: analyzer-reads (burst once a frame, parked: another client's write asks a frame on a microtask and that frame shows it, unread channel asks nothing, one watch per catalog, none after unmount), plugins.test (list, guard, unsubscribe, removal), funscript (g) parked and paused: 28-29 ms push to row. check, check:funscript, --osc, --live-playback green.

title: Funscript analyzer lagOf: about 16 ms/s of CPU, 110 MB per 20 s and the long tasks while the analyzer is open and playing
description: Measured on lp/perf3 (stallprobe with an analyzer-open scene, valencesim, 60 Hz headless, 20 s playing, git-ignored test/evidence/ph-perf3/): with the analyzer open, analyzer.js lagOf takes about 320 ms of CPU and allocates about 110 MB per 20 s, the largest cost on the page. It runs every LAG_EVERY_MS (500 ms) while the trace grows, twice (u and p), each a full scan of 251 shifts over every fresh trace point, so it lands as 8-14 tasks over 12 ms per 20 s (none with the analyzer shut). Options: scan only the trace's recent window, a coarse-to-fine shift search, or the two keys in one pass; and no per-point allocation in the inner loop. Separately, timeline.js traceLines allocates 29 MB (shut) and 73 MB (open) per 20 s while playing.
close_reason: lp/perf4 1d22a74 (unmerged). createLag(key): per-point errors at every shift kept from first sight (pooled), sums rebuilt in trace order, lagOf's answer to the bit (tested over a growing, trimmed, reset trace and a new T). traceLines: frame of reference and drawn window apart; the trace drawn over the slide span under its transform; a point's text kept per frame of reference; join buffers per key and line. stallprobe, concurrent A/B vs 069d253, mean of 2: analyzer open rAF 50.1 -> 37.1 ms/s, main 283.9 -> 273.1, minor GC 8 -> 0, long tasks 3 -> 0; shut rAF 33.7 -> 32.2. --prof: lagOf 230 ms + 110 MB per 20 s -> 27 ms, under 2 MB; traceLines 29 -> 13 MB shut, 71 -> 14 MB open. check, check:funscript, --osc, --live-playback green.

title: Plugin host value() and gate() still allocate per $state proxy read on the per-frame path; the funscript analyzer calls value() per row every frame
description: Measured on lp/perf2 after ph-54gs (raw samples), valencesim, 60 Hz headless, stallprobe --prof, 20 s playing: the Svelte proxy get trap still allocates 21 MB (was 22.8), of which the plugin host's value() 7.4 MB (was 7.9) and gate() 1.8 MB (1.6, noise). The new-sample proxies were not the main cost. Mechanism (test/evidence/ph-perf2/keybench2.mjs, svelte 5.56.8 proxy() under node): every read through a $state proxy allocates 56 B, with or without a source created, and a nested read 112 B; a plain object read allocates 0 (V8's proxy [[Get]] result check builds a property descriptor). A value() call still reads machine.samples (machine proxy), [channel] (samples proxy) and shadows[uid] (shadowOf), plus every field.* read when the field is a proxy. The multiplier is the funscript analyzer: kinetic() runs every frame and calls value() for each tuning row (rows2.find over x.f.role is another 2.7 MB). Options: (1) the analyzer reads its row values once per change (a sample arrival on the tuning channel or a draft edit), not per frame (plugin-local, the multiplier); (2) the host's sample dep reads a raw mirror outside a tracking context ($effect.tracking()) and machine.samples inside one; (3) the analyzer rows hold raw fields (byRole holds raw objects). Needs its own before/after with the stallprobe.
notes:
Probe and bench are lane scratch (lp/perf2, git-ignored): test/evidence/ph-perf2/stallprobe.mjs (the ph-3w4u stallprobe, sim path absolute), dump.mjs + stacks.mjs (heap profile by call stack), keybench2.mjs (bytes per proxy read).
Superseded by lp/perf3 40680e2 (coordinator: no 250 ms staleness). api.changed (experimental, PLUGINS.md): a plain per-channel sequence (src/model/changes.js), bumped on a channel's STATE (machine.svelte.js) and, for every channel, on a link/tier/staleness/latch/rail-owned/shadow/catalog change (an effect in plugins.svelte.js); the motion lock's take and lapse folded in by host.js. The analyzer reads only when its channels' sum moves: zero host reads on unchanged frames, the read on the frame after any change. A Halt does not grey the tuning rows: a setting's gate (plugins.svelte.js gate, Field.svelte) names link, tier and the machine's mask, never the latch; the (g) check asserts they stay writable. stallprobe vs main 278c28b (concurrent, mean of 2): playing shut rAF 33.9 -> 31.3 ms/s, main 234.7 -> 232.3; open rAF 61.3 -> 49.7, main 285.0 -> 275.5, minor GC 11.5 -> 7.5. --prof proxy get trap: playing 23.8 -> 13.5 MB, open 51.7 -> 13.7, paused 24.3 -> 10.8; no analyzer frame left in any proxy stack.
close_reason: lp/perf3 7205861 (unmerged, on main 278c28b). Option 1, local to the plugin: the analyzer reads the hub (row values; open: status, gate, tooltip, trial mark; the Kinetic roles not on a row) at most every 250 ms and at once after a draft, a write, Apply or Discard, a new catalog or an open; a frame that skips its read gets one more when due, so a change made elsewhere shows within 250 ms of a frame. Render inputs and key rebuilt only on a read or a new T; rows paint only on a read. ui.js: one comment line. stallprobe (valencesim, 60 Hz headless, 20 s, concurrent A/B, mean of 2): playing shut rAF 43.7 -> 39.2 ms/s, main 270 -> 266; playing open rAF 72.3 -> 55.6 ms/s, main 318 -> 310, minor GC 11.5 -> 8.5. --prof: proxy get-trap garbage playing shut 23.0 -> 14.4 MB, open 50.8 -> 15.5 MB; host value() 6.0 -> 1.7 (shut), 6.4 -> 1.6 (open); the analyzer's gate/status/stale/reason reads (about 18 MB open) gone. value() is no longer hot: what is left is ui.js realShare and the controller tick (about 0.3 MB each). The largest proxy allocators left are kernel-side: PluginSlot's watch effect (3.0 MB, every claimed-field arrival) and the kernel gate() through the player's per-update status (about 2 MB). Open analyzer: lagOf is the big one, ph-jem5. check, check:funscript, --osc, --live-playback green.

title: RFC-094 fold orphaned saved layouts for the old Tuning (cat9) and Library (cat5) pages; migrate them into Motion and System
description: From the RFC-094 landing (79896da): tab ids machine/valence kept existing layouts, but any layout saved for the retired category pages (cat9 tuning, cat5 library) is now orphaned. On load, fold cat9 placements into the Motion page layout and cat5 into System, below existing cards (first free rect, DESIGN 10.6), once, then delete the old keys. Node test with a fixture layout holding both.
notes: 2026-10-10 lp/hygiene: NOT implemented, pushed back for a ruling. Superseded by the 2026-10-05 ruling (DESIGN 10.6, c6015f9 ph-mdqo.9): the Dash is the only customizable page; a category page lays out from the rank seed and never reads saved placements (DashGrid.svelte seeded = !given && !editable -> place(all, {}, ...)). So full.cat2/full.cat13 are themselves inert, and folding cat9/cat5 into them writes data nothing reads. Deleting the old keys also contradicts law 10 (grid.js: an id the items lack stays inert in storage, never deleted; DESIGN 10.6: placements saved before stay inert). Dash keys (view 'machine') are control keys (role/uid, hero:, widget:, safety:), not category-keyed, so the fold orphaned nothing on the Dash. Group ids also changed (group:9:<name> -> group:2:<name>), so a key move alone would not have matched. Suggest closing as superseded.
close_reason: Superseded: since DESIGN 10.6 (2026-10-05, c6015f9) category pages lay out from the rank seed and never read saved placements, so migrating cat9/cat5 into cat2/cat13 writes data nothing reads; law 10 keeps old placements inert, never deleted. Coordinator call 2026-10-10, veto-able.

comments.text: RFC-089 LANDED in Valence at 44c52b8 (2026-10-07). title: Test hygiene: S3-era live probes, missing fixture etag, no single device-free test entry
description:
MISSING: the live probes default to a SlopDrive-32-era address (valence-live.mjs:17 `--ip 192.168.1.229`) and several (position-jitter-probe, streamed-outlier-probe, og-reference-shots, wire-forensics) measure the retired S3/RP pipeline. README promises test/fixtures/valencesim-catalog.{bin,etag}, but only the .bin exists here (Valence has both). EVIDENCE: test/valence-live.mjs:14-18, README.md test table and fixture note, `ls test/fixtures`, package.json scripts.

ACCEPTANCE: live probes take the hub address with no baked default; obsolete S3-era probes are deleted (with a C-9 proof in the commit) or re-targeted at Nucleus; the fixture pair is re-copied byte-for-byte from Valence; `npm test` runs every device-free suite (check, valence-wire, telebuf-sim, check:shell, check:dash, and the render matrix once it exists) and fails on any failure.
notes: Fixed in 1843ccc: removed baked default host (192.168.1.229) from 14 live probes (now error with usage instead of defaulting); added npm test (device-free: check + valence-wire + telebuf-sim, stop-on-first-failure) and npm run test:browser (check:shell/dash/responsive); rewrote README Tests table with a needs column, one row per test/*.mjs; corrected the stale fixture note (captured from Nucleus sim via valence-sim.mjs, not copied from Valence).
